Zeffon.title: Fruitless Harvest Moon
Zeffon.about:
i. Fruitless Harvest Moon
Though some think I'm crazy
While others deem me insane
I cannot help but continue
And believe it eases my pain
Believe in the harvest moon
Yet I am old and weary
And the light it gives, though fair
Bodes ill will and malevolence
Take care
Beware
Don't trust the harvest moon
The moonlight controls my thoughts
Plus something I cannot see
Sound the alarm, do anything you can
Keep it away from me
Run from the harvest moon
Keep your bravery, boy!
Don't let me down
Take this lantern, prepare the sirens
Warn the entire town
Protect from the harvest moon...
~ A poem written by Governor No. 8 of Lavu on his deathbed.
I apologize for the inconsistencies that occur in my story right about here, but my mind is still a little bit fuzzy on the details. Apparently, mind control can have lasting effects on people like me. In short, my friend turned about to be Reve Terra Lyeon, the second daughter of Reve Isga. How she managed to appear there was beyond me. When I woke up, she interrogated me. She was trying to find her mother, and apparently, as she told me, she couldn't pry this information out of me with her mind powers alone. I knew this wasn't true, but I played along anyway, given that she could melt my brain with a wave of her psychic hand. I told her everything I knew about her father, a man named Kerragan Cathrop. Reve thanked me for my cooperation. As she mentioned, her mother had erased the memory of Uaa and Emeroch Isga, who were in prison for their crimes. Adelais and Lydia Isga, who were also psychics, were above her and she could not decode their thoughts. They simply said it was best for her mother to remain forgotten, but Reve wouldn't let it go.
ii. Dark Columns
Uaa Isga, or Dränsilane, as he would probably rather be known, never really liked his adopted sister as far as I've heard. According to rumors that I've overheard in Blueheart, he was planning to kill his brother Emeroch. According to these rumors, Emeroch is currently infected with a violent strain of Gondii Yelvyn, stage two of the Gondii Maledicta virus that became an issue in Sharhodeon before the country was destroyed. I wish I understood more about it, because Gondii Maledicta was bad enough. In any case, it has been said that Gondii Yelvyn is dependent on the presence of light on its host; the parasite dies, terminating its victim and itself if it does not have any form of light.
iii. Valley
Dränsilane is named as such because of his origins. He had a unique condition that caused his body to decompose around the start of his adult years. This is supposedly a curse, brought on by the recent creation of Castle Adelais. Devastated, the Unkardian Royal Family smashed their daughter's castle to pieces, spreading the fragments far and wide. Dränsilane retreated to what is only known as Valley 65, which is the oddly named valley in the country of Verimore. In its center, there is a town named Crüdza.
iv. Submarine
Dränsilane later returned to Unkardia after his visit to Verimore, after his mother and father had died. He banished Reve his adopted sister. When Emeroch resisted, Dränsilane supposedly drowned him. However, Emeroch survived and swam to the isle of Anne, visibly affected by the encounter. However, I have to stop here.
v. Blue Moon
I would explain more, but I've contained myself in this room for too long. Whenever someone tries to decipher the secrets of Zeffon, there's a fell beast that comes after each individual and maims them in the most cruel and contorted ways. That's the entire reason we as the Lavulese government are so secretive: there's consequences and safety hazards for those who do not comply, not from us, but from powers unknown.
vi. Attic (Sound the Alarm)
At this point, I plan on staying mum on the matters of Zeffon. The main reason I bother to write this down is anyone's guess, but I feel as though these things should be documented in the right ways. A primal fear of the unknown will hopefully not dissuade others from doing the same. I will say this however: do not venture too far into the shadows of the unknown, as you never know what's lurking in the dark. Reve Isga knew it. Her daughters and son knew it. Uaa Isga knew it. Yet, we as humans seem to relish the idea of danger and hazards. The fact that I'm still writing is a sign of that.
vii. Circle of Fear
However, I do want to finish my story about Reve's daughter, Reve Terra Lyeon. She told me to never inquire too deep into the unknown. Although I have always been a curious, inquisitive individual, I decided that it was best to listen to her. I didn't know what it was, but when she started to talk about the unknown, I began to feel rather cold, like there was something gnawing at the bones underneath my skin. I knew it wasn't her and her psychic abilities. It was something else, something undefinable, yet malevolent. This, the feeling told me, was one of many beings in a state of semi-existence, and I was to remain silent about the various things I had seen. I accepted the command, but I have felt compelled to write on these things nevertheless. In any case, goodbye. I hope dearly that these writings will mean nothing bad for me in the long run.

Zeffon.title: Generys Miasma
Zeffon.about:
i. Clay Pots
"The difference between two coins with the first being the sum of one and two twice: this is the key to Dränsilane's will. The second number is always peaceful. The first is not." That's what the spirits say underneath the Temple of Faces. I'm not entirely sure what it all means, but I've ventured down to the 8th floor before and heard the whispers.
Fire Samantabhadrī.
ii. Generys
Generys Miasma is about a village of people north of the Kingdom of Lavu. They eventually established themselves, but they constantly lived in fear of the forest surrounding them, and the malevolence it boded. The leading family controlled the village, and had just had a daughter named Sarah. Tribesmen in the woods however, grew increasingly hostile. Nowadays, there's nothing left, save for a curious glowing spiral in the dirt. This landmark became known as Heayth's Spiral.
iii. Stranger Lands
Few who'd stayed on to establish the CIA in 1947 were all gone. Ames's moment of death may last for three and a half days, generally one.
iv. Prospekti Ritual
In a sense, I've always though the Temple of Faces was an interesting place to go. The main entrance lies inside the Crüdza Well. Following the well down to the bottom leads to an eerily lit swamp where there are a lot of frogs, but also a strange insect-like creature who apparently destroyed the village at Heayth's Spiral. The creature is very docile, but can be irate. It supposedly originated down on the 10th floor of the Temple of Faces, where a lot of the minor beasts of Zeffon are born. Major, or more malevolent beasts usually spawn on the 25th floor. On the 49th floor, there is a door that leads to the Black Room, which is the source of all evil.
v. Miasma
Now, the insect-creature I mentioned before hates one thing above all else: the sound of wind in the trees. That's one reason it has created the odd swamp below the earth where there is no wind. However, the village that used to exist where Heayth's Spiral is called Saroc had this sound near it all the time. Given that there is an entrance to the temple of faces near the ruins of Saroc, the creature could not bear to have Saroc exist. It emerged from its lair and attack the village, with nearby tribesmen taking advantage of the chaos to loot what was left. There were two survivors however: Pana, a young man, and Sarah, the daughter of the leading family.
vi. Sarah's Burial
Due to the conditions of the North, mist enveloped a lot of the forest around the Ruins of Saroc. This happened to a degree that the mist blocked out any air for the two survivors to breathe. Pana went missing for a week while he was searching for food. Sarah quickly became ill due to the oncoming mist and died before Pana returned. Pana buried Sarah near the river, the only place the mist seemed to avoid.
vii. Shadowreaper
A wanderer named Tucker found the ruins of Saroc and began to search for clues as to what happened to the village, when he stumbled upon Sarah's shallow grave. Pana's corpse was lying on the soil, as he had recently passed on. Tucker looked about the clearing, and then he saw a strange cloaked figure that beckoned that it follow him.
viii. Second Illness
The figure pointed at a small valley that it had led Tucker to and then vanished. Tucker suddenly grew violently ill at the sight of it, with small graves with tiny rocks as headstones littered about the clearing. The mist suddenly enveloped Tucker, and soon, he too died.
ix. Ratayu
In the only other village around Saroc, there was a great fire. This village was known as Onis, and no one survived the mysterious blaze except for one young girl and her brother. The brother Isaac quickly grew sick due to the mist, and the girl carried her weakened brother to the spot near the river so that the mist would not follow them. It worked, and the young boy recovered. It was very common for people to get sick due to the mist, but it had never been so thick before. Knowing the way to the capital city of the North called Ratayu, the girl (named Teran) told her brother to wait near the river so that he would not get sick. She disappeared into the mist towards Ratayu to get help.
x. Colony of Ants
When Teran arrived in Ratayu, she was very ill. The mist had flowed into the town and there were corpses everywhere of people who had met a similar fate. She eventually went to the capital building to see if anyone was alive there. Unfortunately, everyone was dead, including the leaders of Ratayu. "It had appeared suddenly", said a note on the town leader's desk. "We were unprepared for this much mist".
xi. Opaque II
Teran returned to the river where she found Isaac still alive. He seemed hungry, but he also seemed to be relatively at peace. Issac noted that the mist did not dare venture near the river for some reason, and the two wondered why that might be.
xii. Latitudelongitude
All in all, Teran and Isaac soon escaped from the bitter problems of the mist. Isaac became one of the Four Brothers, but the story of his escape continued to remain a mystery.

trackinfo.title: Clay Pots
trackinfo.lyrics: i. Clay Pots "The difference between two coins with the first being the sum of one and two twice: this is the key to Dränsilane's will. The second number is always peaceful. The first is not." That's what the spirits say underneath the Temple of Faces. I'm not entirely sure what it all means, but I've ventured down to the 8th floor before and heard the whispers. Fire Samantabhadrī.
trackinfo.credits: from Generys Miasma, released February 24, 2013

trackinfo.title: Generys
trackinfo.lyrics: ii. Generys Generys Miasma is about a village of people north of the Kingdom of Lavu. They eventually established themselves, but they constantly lived in fear of the forest surrounding them, and the malevolence it boded. The leading family controlled the village, and had just had a daughter named Sarah. Tribesmen in the woods however, grew increasingly hostile. Nowadays, there's nothing left, save for a curious glowing spiral in the dirt. This landmark became known as Heayth's Spiral.
trackinfo.credits: from Generys Miasma, released February 24, 2013

trackinfo.title: Strange Lands
trackinfo.lyrics: iii. Stranger Lands Few who'd stayed on to establish the CIA in 1947 were all gone. Ames's moment of death may last for three and a half days, generally one.
trackinfo.credits: from Generys Miasma, released February 24, 2013

trackinfo.title: Prospekti Ritual
trackinfo.lyrics: iv. Prospekti Ritual In a sense, I've always though the Temple of Faces was an interesting place to go. The main entrance lies inside the Crüdza Well. Following the well down to the bottom leads to an eerily lit swamp where there are a lot of frogs, but also a strange insect-like creature who apparently destroyed the village at Heayth's Spiral. The creature is very docile, but can be irate. It supposedly originated down on the 10th floor of the Temple of Faces, where a lot of the minor beasts of Zeffon are born. Major, or more malevolent beasts usually spawn on the 25th floor. On the 49th floor, there is a door that leads to the Black Room, which is the source of all evil.
trackinfo.credits: from Generys Miasma, released February 24, 2013

trackinfo.title: Miasma
trackinfo.lyrics: v. Miasma Now, the insect-creature I mentioned before hates one thing above all else: the sound of wind in the trees. That's one reason it has created the odd swamp below the earth where there is no wind. However, the village that used to exist where Heayth's Spiral is called Saroc had this sound near it all the time. Given that there is an entrance to the temple of faces near the ruins of Saroc, the creature could not bear to have Saroc exist. It emerged from its lair and attack the village, with nearby tribesmen taking advantage of the chaos to loot what was left. There were two survivors however: Pana, a young man, and Sarah, the daughter of the leading family.
trackinfo.credits: from Generys Miasma, released February 24, 2013

trackinfo.title: Sarah's Burial

This happened to a degree that the mist blocked out any air for the two survivors to breathe. Pana went missing for a week while he was searching for food. Sarah quickly became ill due to the oncoming mist and died before Pana returned. Pana buried Sarah near the river, the only place the mist seemed to avoid.

Zeffon.title: Geno Radiativ Toxa
Zeffon.about:
i. Exit Time
That previous story, though strange, is actually true. Once I ran away from Kelios, I honestly didn't expect to survive without shelter, but I did. Eventually, I was picked up by a bunch of pirates who saw me on the shore. I was taken to Fairion in a country known as Oasis. I was far beyond the reach of Lavu, Unkardia, and any other entity that was posed to do me harm.
ii. Tadpole
We arrived in Fairion, which is a town of interesting background: it's been the site of many regicides and the diplomats from Lavu have been systematically murdered as well. Basically, anyone who thought they were above the townsfolk usually got what was coming to them. The pirates that took me in eventually became my close companions, and I wound up a pirate myself, seeing no reason not to do so.
iii. One Thousand
Eventually, we pirates came up with a plan to exact revenge on Uaa, since he had tortured some of the kin of Fairion (via his port town of Cathrop), and I didn't think too highly of my uncle as well. The pirates let me in on a secret of theirs: they had conspired against the Unkardian Royal Family for generations, but had had better things to do instead of attack them. They told me not to worry about the specifics of what those "better things" were.
iv. Dr. Havas
Eventually, I met up with one of their friends: Dr. Havas. Dr. Havas was a laid-back man with little to no concern about his association with Lavu. He said that he had abandoned that empire a long time ago and had arrived in Oasis about five years prior. He seemed to enjoy using my time when I asked about how to find Uaa. Uaa was imprisoned by a secret society after he was caught, but no one could figure out where. It is said that he is underneath the Fair Tower, but the sheer existence of the Fair Tower has been drawn into question. Nevertheless, we decided to make our priority to find the old tower and put Uaa down. In any case, we had to plan carefully. Uaa was a powerful psychic as far as we knew, and he had to be dealt with carefully. Dr. Havas simply smiled and showed me a book he had found in the old government ruins in Fairion - Geno Radiativ Toxa. In the dusty pages, there was apparently a secret weapon.
v. Alien Music
Eventually, we did manage to kill Uaa, which allowed my mother Reve to return home. It did beg the question however: how did all this come to pass? The answer lies in something my former uncle referred to as "instinct". I have to be honest: my uncle was not what he seemed or wanted to be, as many legends (and even I) attest to.
vi. Stuka-food
As he put it, "A fattest man can run on water and the skin of the terrible man can repel fire". Basically, anything can be done if one's senses are in tune with their surroundings. Rumor says that Uaa developed none of these things and grew frustrated, taking much of it out on the population of the isle of Anne. Uaa, or Dränsilane, as he preferred to be known as, was not an evil lord in the stereotypical sense. He was a psychic, but he was fat vegetable of a man, possibly fatter than tall. As such, he could not leave the castle, much less escape from his bedroom. Eventually, he went insane and pushed all his furniture against the door, keeping himself isolated from the world. He had a tendency to talk to birds, especially robins.
vii. Microwave Radiation
In the end though, he screwed up a lot of the different aspects of Zeffon, inventing a history for himself as an evil god. He was evil - he killed many innocent people - he simply did not have the capacity to become such a legend, due to sickness of mind and body. Emeroch is dead as well - Uaa killed him in prison.
viii. Straump Trousse
I did in fact talk to my mother Reve once she returned. If Uaa was such a slob and faker, why did she spend that time guarding him in the Fair Tower? The answer, she told me, lay in the creation of a New God: Straump Trousse. Every time, she said, that people create a new energy, something must be done to harness that energy - and thus a being is born. I had no idea what she was talking about. My mother seemed to be dreadfully ill at this point - something about the odd circumstances of this new energy seemed to have affected her mental state.
ix. The Plant of Life
I met with my sisters Madeline and Reve later on. They had also seen mother and seemed concerned. I had no idea what to make of these things, but I for one am glad that she's all right. She now lives in Lavu, and she seems to be slowly regaining her sanity, but there's something about Fair Tower that rubbed me the wrong way when I first saw it. It's a tower made of yellow sulfur-like stone that was constructed during the time of Fair Onrac, the boy of curse. As far as I'm aware, no one really knows who Fair Onrac was, but they say it was his curse that completely ruined Inejeheim. According to legend, he was a young boy when he found a chunk of Castle Adelais that had been brought back through time. Growing out of the clammy grey stone was a plant, and this is said to have set the stage for Zeffon's eternal curse.

Zeffon.title: Glorious Jala
Zeffon.about:
i. Glorious Jala
The name of a continent that has been under Ratayu's influence has been long since forgotten. There used to be a great civilization on Jala, which has been reduced to nothing but a small frontier town. That frontier town is known as Barra. Surprisingly, despite Jala's isolation, many people decide to live on this continent, as it has many unexplored regions and untapped resources.
ii. Frontier Town of Barra
The frontier town of Barra has, at times, seen better days, but people who live in it seem able to make a living. Among the curiosities in Barra is the Old Inn, a traveler's best dream. Although the people of Barra sometimes claim that nightmares seem prevailent in the aging town, travelers always sleep soundly, waking and saying they never felt better. In the middle of Barra, there's an old house that belongs to the innkeeper however. According to rumors, the innkeeper dares not sleep in her own inn.

Zeffon.title: Graghgorra
Zeffon.about:
i. Unkardiad (Lord of the Flies)
In the dimension Graghgorra, fears can manifest themselves as large malevolent beings, capable of destroying the person from which they are derived. In fact, Graghgorra is the oldest dimension out of many, being about as old as the Earth. Although the beings in Graghgorra cannot cross the dimensional rift into our world, they can feed upon the human overmind, a large amoeba-like flan of sorts. Each human on Earth is psychically represented by a cell in the human overmind. If a cell dies, its respsective human does as well...
In the moon, there is a secret cave. Inside said cave, there is a well - a well that contains the origins of all life here in Zeffon. Whether you choose to believe me or not is up to you.
In the swamps and marshes of the west, there is a bell tower of an old forgotten church that slowly continues to sink into the abyss. Here they say, men come and perform devilish rituals in the name of the Old God of Crüdza. Crüdza is a very ancient town that lies in modern-day Verimore that is oft omitted on maps. An old map from four centuries ago still confirms its existence. The deep well in the middle of the abandoned town leads to a marshy land full of decaying trees. Theorists have it that the old people of Crüdza built the church to convert people who lived there - that is, if the people who lived there still exist. There's rumors of a large cockroach-like insect that patrols the muddy lands in search for prey. The longer people stay out of the well, the hungrier it gets, until it finally emerges and goes on a rampage. Aside from small rodents and the like, it is said that it poses no threat to humans.
ii. Human Bradyzoites, Pt. 1
In the well, it's almost like another world: there's an incredible amount of light for something that is completely underground, and it is said that a lot of this comes from the misty green waters that bubble up from the earth's core. It's unknown what these pools are made of, but it is generally concluded that they are the source of an eerie mist that wafts from the valley every morning. The mist seems to drive people mad, and a condensed solid version of this mist is said to be the material from which the Bell of Noor is made.
iii. Graghgorra
If the earth is really so deep, why haven't we discovered it yet? The answer lies with the ancient Ognians, the original residents of Unkardia, where mist flows like a fluid river. They guard an ancient foe that came from an unknown place. The Temple of Faces for example: if one ventures too deep, they will be torn apart by old Ognian guards. It's not necessarily their own will that causes them to guard what lies beneath the earth.

Zeffon.title: Grey Fascination
Zeffon.about:
- An album assembled from small recordings that were made in 2006/7 (Tracks 4-6 were made in 2014). Although the titles and artwork are not genuine (not created back then), the music tracks themselves are authentic. This is the only record (so far), of the ancient phase of Zeffon (a history of what occurred before the war that tore apart Lavu and initiated Dränsilane's stay in the Frogplain). Dränsilane went by many names, but is more commonly referred to by a number during his dreams. This number was 2510.
i. Dragänsword
I watched helplessly as Dränsilane was taken away by his father Norfell. Dränsilane had broken the code of Unkardia, and was thus bound for Du Garma Canyon. Although we held a fortress close to the feature, I knew that there was something else going when I saw my brother tied to a wooden beam that was placed on a boat. They were heading off the island, somewhere that none of us knew about. I was imprisoned in the Castle Deeps for my "insolence", or my inquires as to where they were taking him. It's awfully cold down here, and I hear something moving in the dark. My one candle that was granted to me is about to go out. The whole character of this "would you like a candle" makes me think this is more of an execution than an imprisonment. Well, goodbye to whoever finds this on the wall, if anyone ever does. I sense my time is at an end...
ii. Tribal Decay Dance
I do understand why WHL ran away. For this to be true, she must have communed with deep statues.
iii. Creative Lunacy
WILL was the ancient king that surrounded the temple and town with his guardian stones of Ann.
iv. Opëillajja (Creative Lunacy Remix, 2014)
I had a vision KO to annihilate the entirety of the corruption surrounding your lies.
v. Killing Fields (Asma pain_ for deep thought)
OZ continues to resist the temptation brought upon by WLL to come to of the foot.
vi. Lotus
To overrun the prophets of the time spent is to overrun the ideas that issue from imagination of Leplayh-WILL.

Zeffon.title: Grievances
Zeffon.about:
i. Discovery
Grievances is the fourth in Kerragan's dream sequences. This one is about the fall of a very modernized society and how they're related to Kerragan's generation.
Félix Oarr predicted the demise of this world by my hand. In fact, trying to keep one of many incarnations of myself imprisoned drained much of his sanity. I didn’t even try to escape at times. It was hilarious to watch that hideous man try in vain. But even in his insanity, although I hate to admit it, he did drain some of my power. He was also the one who found a way to preserve time.
ii. An Ominous Daybreak
By sending a clone back into time to stop son from affecting everything I had worked for, the mindless puppet developed a mind of its own, and instead of capturing Vari Cathrop and killing him, it guided Reve, who was originally my wife, to follow it and rebel against me, its Creator. Soon, the two killed me, and I was back to square one with yet another ominous daybreak. Essentially, time reset itself after I was killed, setting the year back to when I had created it.
iii. Carpet Bombing
Félix had taken advantage of the fact that I created time to be from my perspective, and had manipulated me with his experiments so I would willingly get killed. As much as I hate to admit it, he was very clever.
iv. radioFUTURE
But his sanity would eventually drain due to the fact that time looped like this for 513 times. On time 514, he was so mentally incompetent that he was committed to an insane asylum, before he was murdered by my accomplice, Derek Umattias, or as he calls himself, Dr. Uy. Once again, there was no hope for the world, and I was back on track.
v. Wooden Teeth
However, you would never believe how hard it is to destroy your own creations.
vi. Locust
In any case, much to my annoyance and lack of foresight despite being an oracle, I failed to realize that going into the past interrupted the time stream, which inevitably destroyed the future. I have no idea why that did not cross my mind.
vii. Shadows of the Past
However, I have a slight suspicion that it was the doing of D23, the master who created me. D23 exists within 7429FD, the Purple Star. However, 7429FD is not a star by definition. It glows and emits the external behavior of your small Sol, but the inside is actually hollow.
viii. March of the Silverpseudosquares
The inside of the Purple Star was the origin of the entire multiverse: tens of thousands of universes mashed together, each defined by a thin membrane border. If there’s a multiverse outside of this multiverse, then I do not know of it. The fact is that there is a small foundry and factory within the enormous space of this hollow star.
ix. O23
It is O23. The name is what makes me believe that there is a large source, a larger origin outside of this one, the fact that it is “Origin 23”. This may be where the higher powers who created D23 exist. D23 is a biomechanical being that oversees the creation and destruction of O23. I am the regulator that upholds D23’s demands.
x. Grievances
However, I could never live with the idea that I may have a defect. That is why I’m calling on you. You are my hope for the future. I cannot travel anywhere near O23 as long as I exist. As I told you, the universe ends in 6 days as D23 commands. But I’ve discovered a flaw in the creation of time and space for this universe. In the battles between Eresymcaion and Muagara, time is both simultaneously moving and stopped. So for this theory to work, one must treat time as a set of rules. Space is the playing field, but time makes certain that the laws of physics and such are upheld. I need you to travel back in time, erasing everything. Keep trying until you can reach Origin 23 and kill my master.
xi. Block 6
I will become immortal.
Zeffon.credits:
released May 27, 2012
Sound Credits - kijjaz
Everything Else - Creighton Jenkins

Zeffon.title: (he is who I think he is)
Zeffon.about:
i. Moldy Apartment
- (he is who I think he is)
When my master told me that a lesser god had killed himself, I could hardly believe it. Then to learn that it was the insane one...
In any case, I've been watching the apartment for years now, waiting for my boss to reply. He hasn't sent me a letter in weeks, and it's really starting to test my nerves.
Just the other day, some construction crew pulled out some rotten wallpaper out of the place. I heard that one of the few residents renting the apartment (my subject of whom to view from a long distance) had gone mad. If so, mission accomplished. I can go get my pay. The man is dead.
I was going to do some further scouting to make sure that the man truly is dead and that we won't need to worry about him any longer. According to my boss, he's quite powerful, but doesn't know it yet. It's as if he just needs to awaken.
Anyhow, the other day, I went to the apartment at night, the frogs chirping and croaking as usual. I continued on and eventually found myself in the abandoned building opposite the target's residence. As I made my way to the top, I tripped slightly on a step, causing a noise that made the night watchman's flashlight illuminate the ceiling above me through the ruined open window. I simply ducked and everything was okay. Or so I thought.
To tell you the truth, that watchman had always scared me. It was as if he knew when I would be observing the man, whether it was from afar or from across the street. In any case, I slowly and quietly removed my aging rifle components from my pack. The stock seemed weird, it was as if the moist air around me had soaked into it somehow. At the bottom of the pack were my binoculars. Using them to gaze through the open window, I spotted a flickering light. I didn't know what to make of it, but my guess was that the light was on the verge of burning out, like a lantern without any oil. I shuddered, imagining being in a deep forest without any light. It seemed too real a possibility, so I lit the lantern I had with me.
The light from that lantern must have been very visible from the street, because before I knew it, someone was riddling the area with bullets. Leaving my rifle components behind, I ran out with my binoculars and fled into the back alley. I slid into the shadows easily, and soon, I could no longer hear any commotion. Not that there was much to begin with; the streets of these parts of the town didn't have a lot of people in them anyway.
I returned. My rifle parts were gone. However, in their place was a small note.
"Meet me at Karij." That's what it said.
I recognized the handwriting instantly. It was that of my boss.
ii. Pscilocin
Caria is gone to sleep and the meaning of the wiced is lost among the ashes at misty mire.
I discovered later that there was something a little bit odd about how Ratayu was situated in the middle of a desert. I soon saw a plane fly overhead, and I winced at the thought of it dropping bombs on my head. Ever since Caria had that dream in the Forest of Shadow memories, the radios in Ratayu had been filled with strange static and voices talking to one another. Sometimes, the conversations went a bit like this:
"Do you think they're ready?"
"Do you?"
"The shadow won't last long. Perhaps it's time we lay waste."
"Give them longer."
The conversation repeats itself every 15 seconds or so, and then it turns into radio static.
Caria noticed that her grandfather Kerragan had been acting odd since the dream that she had had about her uncle Dränsilane. She had also been feeling a little bit queasy and light-headed after the encounter, but she had managed to shake it off. Her grandfather however, began to complain about voices that he kept hearing. This is when Caria's mother dashed into the room and closed the door behind her.
"Caria..." She looked as though she had seen a ghost.
"Mom? What is it?"
"They're coming..."
Caria suddenly thought she heard a low bump in the desert night outside. It was barely audible, but with her hearing, she could confirm that yes, something was out in the desert sands. Something big.
"Mom? What's coming for us?"
Caria closed her eyes and began to think about the sandstorms that would occasionally erupt at night, and with her psychic powers, she saw something that was shrouded in bellowing sand. Upon closer inspection, it seemed like a giant mass of writhing hair, until a human head attached to a very long neck emerged from the mass and turned, looking at Caria with half-decayed eyes, pale, and stray maggots crawling around its crooked eyes. The smell was incredible.
"Breathe this and walk as the living dead..." said a raspy voice.
Caria opened her eyes. Her mom was leaning against the door with her ear to it, as if trying to pinpoint the location of the foul beast.
"Mom? That looked very much like Enöigimras, the Final King of Dotajmari, based on what I've read about him."
"He's beckoning all those who are in Ratayu at the moment to follow him to the land of the undead. Caria, you know what happened to your grandmother, yes? She disappeared into thin air. It's likely that that thing out there got her."
"She's a powerful psychic! How could that be the case?"
iii. The Patrolman and his Lonely Duties
Sleep my puppet, for the end is nigh. Do not contain te differe. that your cl. sees.

I was going to do some further scouting to make sure that the man truly is dead and that we won't need to worry about him any longer. According to my boss, he's quite powerful, but doesn't know it yet. It's as if he just needs to awaken. Anyhow, the other day, I went to the apartment at night, the frogs chirping and croaking as usual. I continued on and eventually found myself in the abandoned building opposite the target's residence. As I made my way to the top, I tripped slightly on a step, causing a noise that made the night watchman's flashlight illuminate the ceiling above me through the ruined open window. I simply ducked and everything was okay. Or so I thought. To tell you the truth, that watchman had always scared me. It was as if he knew when I would be observing the man, whether it was from afar or from across the street. In any case, I slowly and quietly removed my aging rifle components from my pack. The stock seemed weird, it was as if the moist air around me had soaked into it somehow. At the bottom of the pack were my binoculars. Using them to gaze through the open window, I spotted a flickering light. I didn't know what to make of it, but my guess was that the light was on the verge of burning out, like a lantern without any oil. I shuddered, imagining being in a deep forest without any light. It seemed too real a possibility, so I lit the lantern I had with me. The light from that lantern must have been very visible from the street, because before I knew it, someone was riddling the area with bullets. Leaving my rifle components behind, I ran out with my binoculars and fled into the back alley. I slid into the shadows easily, and soon, I could no longer hear any commotion. Not that there was much to begin with; the streets of these parts of the town didn't have a lot of people in them anyway. I returned. My rifle parts were gone. However, in their place was a small note. "Meet me at Karij." That's what it said. I recognized the handwriting instantly. It was that of my boss.

Zeffon.title: Heesarotruna
Zeffon.about:
i. Mero
Zeffon is a world devastated by conflict, whether it be through the powers of darkness, light, peace, genocide, etc. Every single person uses conflict to tilt the outcome of politics and society in their favor. Some people are trapped in the middle however, and just want to have a way to live. Some are tired. In a town called Mero, the people resisted their government's attempts to lock up anyone associated with "anarchist" group.
ii. Everfrost
Some backstory: there is a group of "collaborators of retailers" who "dared" to suggest that the government that oversaw Mero's affairs was treating these individuals unfairly. There were more outspoken members of this protest and some radicalized ones that persisted in creating a volatile situation for the government. These radical individuals became the face of the movement according to the wishes of the government's leadership.
iii. Gnata-Musca
Many of these people were told to work in the factories, and that all of their past acts of disobedience would be forgotten if they were to simply continue about their daily lives. Given that the daily lives of some of these collaborators were in tatters, they figured they had nothing to lose. The rest were obligated to assist their comrades.
iv. Hostage
I feel it's important to analyze the situation from a distance and not react emotionally to the affairs of others. However, I'm frequently called out for being lethargic and unwilling to understand the problems that afflict our society as a whole, as long as they don't affect me personally.
v. Inside Heresh Mel - A Noll
Eventually, I decided to visit the Ruins of Null, the place where my ancestors were born. According to my inherent beliefs and the belief that my family holds, the Ruins of Null answer the questions of those who dare to ask them.
vi. Feeling Far Away
"The power of expression is a great thing. Do not let it go to waste." This is what the spirits of the ruins told me. "Control your thoughts to avoid being led astray." This is also the essence of the voices. I understood what the voices meant, but misunderstood how to execute the solutions presented.
vii. Anthim of Glouries R.Stevce K.
Soon I felt uncomfortable. I didn't understand where I was, or how I got there, but I got the impression that I was phasing in and out of existence, like someone was trying to draw me into their world. With great mental effort, I escaped.
viii. Heesarotruna
Suddenly, I woke up. It was a dream. But it felt very real. Living in this dimension, I had learned to question reality, as many things start happening to those who trust everything to be the way it seems. That said, I got out of bed and walked to the secret room in my apartment. When I arrived inside the room, I sat down next to my mother Reve. She had been asleep ever since we brought her to this town, and I didn't blame her. Keeping Uaa Isga sealed beneath an ancient tower obviously did things to her mind and available energy.
ix. Katella
However, I couldn't escape the sensation that all was not well. Some odd sounds could be heard in the night. It wasn't creepy in the sense of creating a scare for everyone, but it sounded oddly familiar. I had no idea why until my aunt Lydia came by.
x. Rast Mronfastioa
Lydia told me that there had been other people that had undergone tragedies that Unkardia had nothing to do with. As my aunt continued to talk, I couldn't help but notice that she hadn't aged a day. Then she mentioned a man named Isaac. The name struck me with the same familiarity that the odd sound in the night did.
xi. Cethrinyk Lave
Finally, I asked Lydia how she was doing. She replied that she was doing well and thanked me for my consideration. I finally couldn't resist talking to Lydia about her mysteries, as I hadn't seen her in a long time, and I asked about how she stayed young, presenting it as a curious question.
xii. Rast Urt
Lydia smiled and said that I wasn't even born when Uaa convinced the Creator to bless her, Adelais, and Mathilda with eternal life. She said that Uaa used to be a kind man, but his wish sacrificed a lot of the goodness within him. Either that, or it fatigued the goodness so that the evil beneath was exposed. Lydia told me that she came to check on my mother, and I gave her passage to my mother's room.

Zeffon.about:
With this album, the about half the people leave Vorsanchu in an event known only as "Hemerjia". 27 people fled the town in the middle of the night. Carved on a tree are the words "A Forest", but no one knows which one. Three nights after, when an earthquake hits, the rest of the town of Vorsanchu packs up and moves toward the Eastern Forest. There, they find a stone temple with the 27 people inside. They explain that they saw a strange orange mist that came into Vorsanchu, and suddenly had the instinctive to run to safety. Vorsanchu's location was then lost, given that it was abandoned from that point on.
The track "Attention!!" refers to the Western Forest with a dirt mound in the middle of it where nothing can grow.
Beautiful Stone is about a dream that can be brought upon a sleeper by means of a drumming melody. It is the only way to see into the previous world of Zeffon. Reve Terra Lyeon, with the help of two reluctant drummers, manages to see her uncles and aunts in a castle on Exeräise.
Fern is a dream that Reve Terra Lyeon has of her parents. They say that Reve needs to come and find them, for they are trapped in the deepest darkness. It is the first of a large series of visions.
Mohtetrg refers to the nights of fear of when the first 27 people abandoned Vorsanchu. It ends when the people of Vorsanchu are reunited in the Eastern Forest.
Blackberis Earthquake is about the earthquake that drives the rest of Vorsanchu's citizens into the Eastern Forest.

Zeffon.title: Horror
Zeffon.about:
i. Oármagaon
Horror contains two tracks that were recorded later after the Stormbringer performance, since they were re-discovered after the performance took place. No one knows the significance of the seven new movements.
VII: Catatomentia - Unknown significance. Thought to represent a town sunken in the desert sands west of the Kingdom of Lavu called Oármagaon. Also hypothesized to build off of Movement II: Psychosis.
VIII: Cedij - Represents turmoil in the heavens, as humans fight for an heir for a position of power.
IX: ?
X: ?
After the phonautographs are found for parts 7 and 8 of the Serenade for the Dead, they are stolen by four brothers. These four claim to be representing the "good of humanity", and do everything they can to get in Lavu's way.
~
The abstract
Painting that rests on the far wall
Can only create
A broken, stagnancy
For the wall
The harvest
Can only create a tragedy
There is nothing left for you here
For whether Dr. Uy is Derek or Nathaniel
You
You will never know for sure
Just as the static meets the Shorelines
You will reap what you sow
For you shall know
That whether Uy is D or N
Is something I have made so
Beyond comprehension
Yet a hair's width away
The dimension Graghgorra rests to stay
In this pit of ultimate despair
Lies the Sorrow, the Horror, and the Mare
The Mandras represent everything mad
Yield to the clot that begs to be filled
Garrison behind the wall that begs to be hallowed
Veer from the path that begs to be followed
For those who are not holy
Shall by the Horror be swallowed
The fanatical fiends of the Cedij being
Claw their way to the stairway to the star ceiling
For in the sky lies the key
To the Strait that was discovered by the Gree
In contrast to the river and shore
There is always someone who wants to have more
More of the sadness, the sorrow, the despair
The annoyances promoted by the old Mare
From this eternal abyss of the sadness
Rise the Mandras, who represent madness
Whether or not the traveler will care
Will then determine how they will fare
For the mind's eye is what stands between you
And the other world to be had
Just be sure it will never drive you mad
Come night!
Come day!
Come eternal abyss!
Though the harvest was lost
Though the harvest was lost
Stay your weapons!
Sheathe your swords!
I mean you no harm at all!
You only need to destroy this wall
And then from the laws of the other world
You shall know all.
...This is a poem that was written a long time ago by a very significant poet going by a variety of names. He's known as "The Phantom Artist", as he has had several identities over the course of many years, and many like to say that he assumes these identities because he's a wandering spirit with regrets. He was once a great king by the name of Myrioc Oear. He's invented several names for himself and invented a past for himself as well. Some of his pseudonyms include Unknown Iahae, Ha Ma, Harris, among others. He's known to play guitar in a canyon that is in the middle of Mödgod, the continent that has the once-great kingdom of Inejeheim as the jewel to its crown. In any case, people say that his poems are prophetic, which is why I include them in this volume.
ii. Legend of Desmemon
This particular poem I believe is important. I have no idea why that may be, since a great many do not understand the writings of King Myrioc Oear. I selected this one because of its mention of "the mind's eye", which can mean many things. One of the things that it could refer to, which is specifically relevant to the folks in Blueheart, is the Nacajda. The Nacajda has been used by Miu to spy on the people who live in Blueheart while they sleep. It is unknown why this is. Supposedly, when Miu was more powerful, he could influence people all the way in Unkardia.
iii. Still The Orchestra Plays
However, I'm a little off-topic here. The man I helped seemed to know something about my dear friend (who will remain anonymous and nameless for now) was taken to an inn in Curja, and I paid for his fee there. While I was there, there were some people who said they had been traumatized by something they had seen from afar at the Nacajda. "Don't go there! You'll regret it! The crown... It's powerful!" They continued to babble like madmen.
iv. VII: Catatomentia
When the soldier finally awoke, he begged me not to go and search for his friends. He said that they were gone, and there was nothing that could be done about it. He did thank me though. After talking with him a bit, he informed me of the danger that his former friends now imposed on the nearby villages. We needed to defend ourselves to the best of our ability, because according to him, there was going to be something happening later that night.
v. VIII: Cedij
It was a rainy night, as are a lot of the nights around Blueheart. Usually there's a strange melodic humming that occurs around the midnight hour, but that was not around this time. There was an ominous presence in the air, something that I had felt only around the Nacajda. It felt as though I was being watched. It suddenly occurred to me that Miu was using the opportunity to spy on the villagers while they slept. As I closed my eyes as the rain came down, I saw the image of a large eye, as if it were painted on the inside of my eyelids. I was initially horrified, but for some reason I cannot yet explain, I was not completely uncomfortable with the presence. It was malevolent and filled the air with a certain heaviness, but it wasn't completely undesirable.

Zeffon.title: Howtriver G00daristatrbasm
Zeffon.about:
i. Howtriver G00daristatrbasm
I realized that there was a problem the instant I went there. The name "Howtriver Goodaristatrbasm" was a code phrase that was meant to be written and not pronounced, but pronouncing it was a necessity when considering that it was the way that the people of Vahn identified themselves as Vahnites at home and abroad.
Vahn is a city on the Isle of Daei, a city built on the ancient plains that exist there from a darker age. The age I am referencing is one filled with violence and strife. Eventually, in order to show solidarity with the idea of peace, the people of Vahn erected statues on the southwest tip of the Isle of Daei, having them looking towards the ancient plains, as if observing. These statues are referenced by the word "Howtriver" in the previously mentioned code phrase, allowing the Vahnites to remind each other of the commitment to peace that they were subject to.
But like I mentioned before, there was a problem.
ii. Grey Sphinx
There is a certain noxious weed that grows in the southwest part of the isles where the statues are. This weed is known as Grey Sphinx, and it is a very powerful plant that stays in the bloodstream for weeks if consumed or made contact with. The people of the Isle of Daei know about it, making sure to stay away. As for the effects of the weed, it makes one lose perception of all color. Again, this lasts for weeks, so this can be a hindrance more so than a nuisance. The problem lies in the fact that Grey Sphinx also creates hallucinatory sounds from days long past, reminding many Vahnites of the far-forgotten days of violence.
iii. Odd Sin
This became an issue when individuals from all over the Isle of Daei were trying to live in peace. The Grey Sphinx, when it flowers, records the sounds that came from that particular day when it was in bloom, often short segments, maybe 13 seconds long. However, these sounds become archived and part of the plant. It is also said that the sounds that the Grey Sphinx hears cause it to be healthy or unhealthy, depending on the sound. The plant is also said to grow inside the earth - how deep is up for investigation.
iv. Sunsackpile
In any case, after a while, the Grey Sphinx that remained on the island withered and died, giving the Vahnites much relief. Life continued as normal, but then something happened that caused the island to be evacuated practically overnight. Around Vahn, there is a giant wall. It is supposed to keep something out. However, one night, a section of the wall mysteriously crumbled without warning, allowing something, whether physical or spiritual, to enter the town. Many Vahnites woke up suddenly, instinctively knowing they were in grave danger. Soon, the city was empty, though it is unknown where the people went off to, as they were on an island.
v. The Silent Man
When one enters the old city of Vahn nowadays, there is a man that patrols the city, telling travelers to leave immediately. Whether alive or dead, the man appears to have been a former king.
vi. Baraqoparti
The earth around Vahn is very mushy nowadays, as if rotting. If one ventures onto the Isle of Daei, the only solid ground that one will not sink into is located where the statues are. The statues that are the monument to the past violence of the Vahnites still stand, albeit crumbling and beyond repair. One can still visit the area of one gets past the stench of the nearby rotting Earth.
vii. The Creature Within the Walls, Scratching Like a Moth
Now, there is a strange piece of land to the north of Vahn that is a wooded area. It is said the the Mandras (a small woodland dwelling people) have an old shrine in there, but no one can verify this, mostly because of the wind that blows through the trees there. The wind is said to take one's spirit, and I believe every word I've heard, after one of my companions ventured in and disappeared forever. However, if one is acquainted with the Mandras, they supposedly can shrink you - to the point where nearby grass shields anyone from the death wind. Naturally, this is called the Wood of the Dead.
I eventually talked to my friend named Lauren, who has been a number of places, including the infamous Library of Anne. She said that, with the help of Lydia and Adelais Isga, managed to meet one of the Mandra shaman elders, who was one of the few that could still use the shrinking spell. Lauren, after being reduced in size, was then guided through the underbrush of the Wood of the Dead by a Mandra guide to the ancient shrine that they called the Jaursibulava Shrine, after the Mandra god of the sky. Inside, there is supposedly a large moth that guards the Wind Element, which is one of two elements that has not been corrupted by Zeffon's negative energy. While the Water and Earth Elements are cursed as of now, the Fire and Wind elements have been hidden and kept safe. Lauren made it out, but told me that there was an occasional scratching that she kept hearing, as if there was something in all the walls making the shrine. In the forest she said as well, there was a single grave about the size of her thumbnail that was huge when the size of a Mandra. On it, reads one name: Vahn.

trackinfo.title: Howtriver G00daristatrbasm
trackinfo.lyrics: i. Howtriver G00daristatrbasm I realized that there was a problem the instant I went there. The name "Howtriver Goodaristatrbasm" was a code phrase that was meant to be written and not pronounced, but pronouncing it was a necessity when considering that it was the way that the people of Vahn identified themselves as Vahnites at home and abroad. Vahn is a city on the Isle of Daei, a city built on the ancient plains that exist there from a darker age. The age I am referencing is one filled with violence and strife. Eventually, in order to show solidarity with the idea of peace, the people of Vahn erected statues on the southwest tip of the Isle of Daei, having them looking towards the ancient plains, as if observing. These statues are referenced by the word "Howtriver" in the previously mentioned code phrase, allowing the Vahnites to remind each other of the commitment to peace that they were subject to. But like I mentioned before, there was a problem.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: Grey Sphinx
trackinfo.lyrics: ii. Grey Sphinx There is a certain noxious weed that grows in the southwest part of the isles where the statues are. This weed is known as Grey Sphinx, and it is a very powerful plant that stays in the bloodstream for weeks if consumed or made contact with. The people of the Isle of Daei know about it, making sure to stay away. As for the effects of the weed, it makes one lose perception of all color. Again, this lasts for weeks, so this can be a hindrance more so than a nuisance. The problem lies in the fact that Grey Sphinx also creates hallucinatory sounds from days long past, reminding many Vahnites of the far-forgotten days of violence.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: Odd Sin
trackinfo.lyrics: iii. Odd Sin This became an issue when individuals from all over the Isle of Daei were trying to live in peace. The Grey Sphinx, when it flowers, records the sounds that came from that particular day when it was in bloom, often short segments, maybe 13 seconds long. However, these sounds become archived and part of the plant. It is also said that the sounds that the Grey Sphinx hears cause it to be healthy or unhealthy, depending on the sound. The plant is also said to grow inside the earth - how deep is up for investigation.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: Sunsackpile
trackinfo.lyrics: iv. Sunsackpile In any case, after a while, the Grey Sphinx that remained on the island withered and died, giving the Vahnites much relief. Life continued as normal, but then something happened that caused the island to be evacuated practically overnight. Around Vahn, there is a giant wall. It is supposed to keep something out. However, one night, a section of the wall mysteriously crumbled without warning, allowing something, whether physical or spiritual, to enter the town. Many Vahnites woke up suddenly, instinctively knowing they were in grave danger. Soon, the city was empty, though it is unknown where the people went off to, as they were on an island.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: The Silent Man
trackinfo.lyrics: v. The Silent Man When one enters the old city of Vahn nowadays, there is a man that patrols the city, telling travelers to leave immediately. Whether alive or dead, the man appears to have been a former king.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: Baraqoparti
trackinfo.lyrics: vi. Baraqoparti The earth around Vahn is very mushy nowadays, as if rotting. If one ventures onto the Isle of Daei, the only solid ground that one will not sink into is located where the statues are. The statues that are the monument to the past violence of the Vahnites still stand, albeit crumbling and beyond repair. One can still visit the area of one gets past the stench of the nearby rotting Earth.
trackinfo.credits: from Howtriver G00daristatrbasm, released September 10, 2017

trackinfo.title: The Creature Within the Walls, Scratching Like a Moth
trackinfo.lyrics: vii. The Creature Within the Walls, Scratching Like a Moth Now, there is a strange piece of land to the north of Vahn that is a wooded area. It is said the the Mandras (a small woodland dwelling people) have an old shrine in there, but no one can verify this, mostly because of the wind that blows through the trees there. The wind is said to take one's spirit, and I believe every word I've heard, after one of my companions ventured in and disappeared forever. However, if one is acquainted with the Mandras, they supposedly can shrink you - to the point where nearby grass shields anyone from the death wind. Naturally, this is called the Wood of the Dead. I eventually talked to my friend named Lauren, who has been a number of places, including the infamous Library of Anne. She said that, with the help of Lydia and Adelais Isga, managed to meet one of the Mandra shaman elders, who was one of the few that could still use the shrinking spell. Lauren, after being reduced in size, was then guided through the underbrush of the Wood of the Dead by a Mandra guide to the ancient shrine that they called the Jaursibulava Shrine, after the Mandra god of the sky. Inside, there is supposedly a large moth that guards the Wind Element, which is one of two elements that has not been corrupted by Zeffon's negative energy. While the Water and Earth Elements are cursed as of now, the Fire and Wind elements have been hidden and kept safe. Lauren made it out, but told me that there was an occasional scratching that she kept hearing, as if there was something in all the walls making the shrine. In the forest she said as well, there was a single grave about the size of her thumbnail that was huge when the size of a Mandra. On it, reads one name: Vahn.

Zeffon.title: HRU 3, the Irritatingly Similar Version of Dental Wôrk
Zeffon.about:
Oscar heard a noise. It was faint at this point, but it was clearly audible at this point. No sooner had he thought to run that the noise stopped, as if it could tell that it had been caught trying to pry into his mind, and had begun to slink into the shadows to avoid further suspicion. Oscar shuddered at the thought of getting caught by one of those mutant catoblepones.
"Help..."
Hearing a voice, Oscar ran to the source of the sound: a heavily built young man lying face up in the muck. His open eyes darted about, and Oscar quickly realized that the man couldn't see him. Upon closer inspection, it was one of the Kell boys.
"Whoev' ya are, get back..." moaned the figure.
A low hum followed by a high ring entered Oscar's ears, meaning the catoblepones were close. Oscar ran as fast as he could, or as fast as anyone can through liquid mud and into what appeared to be a disused barn to hide. There, he found a horrific scene. A human corpse rippling with maggots was situated in the center of the space. A catoblepas was gnawing on a human leg in the corner, its floundering bulbous head moping up any morsels that had been left over. In a small separate compartment in the corner, the sound of a girl shouted at him to enter, and Oscar quickly darted in, puzzled that the catoblepas hadn't seemed to notice him. Beatrice hugged him upon his entry to the small room. Inside, he found his sister and mother Catherine. Mom seemed a little skinny, as if she hadn't eaten in a day or two, but still alive and no worse for wear.

Zeffon.title: HRU 5 (and then seen...)
Zeffon.about:
Oscar headed north, since this was where Kell had his old shack in the dark woods. Whether or not this was still true was probably up for some debate, but Oscar knew that pretty quickly, and he was also pretty sure that if Kell had taken his dad, it would've been to his own house.
After a few days, Oscar found a pike with a skull impaled on it. The family farm was clearly nearby. Breaking through the noisy brush as tenderly as he could, Oscar came to a clearing of poorly tended land marred by single-toed hoofprints. Although Oscar couldn't see any of Them nearby (or in all the separate pastures as far as he could see), a few of the hoofprints seemed very fresh, and it was in his best interest to find Dad, Mom, Bee, and the get out of the area as quickly and quietly as possible. Any stray noise no matter how subtle might startle something.
Making has way along the fence line, Oscar began to become unnerved. An imminent threat of danger wasn't obvious, but the entire farm land gave him chills. Sensing something strange, Oscar turned around and found a dry reed like the one back at the house. This reed crumbled in his hand, like it had been around ages. The scroll that Beatrice had left inside looked as though it had been placed thousands of years ago, turning to dust upon physical contact. Oscar was able to make out the phrase "...ppo or..." before a stray breeze broke what remained of the decrepit parchment. "Ppo" seemed to be the least three letters of a name, but whose? What did Beatrice want to say about this mystery person? A howl in the distance startled Oscar. His ancestor's ability felt diminished, even non-existent here. As he walked cautiously towards one of the barns, he began to shudder as the feeling of ice pooled through his veins.

Zeffon.title: Humpty Dumpty Enz Dêd (The Big Stick VIII)
Zeffon.about: The way is shut, and that is a good thing. After all, we can't have the living dead roaming around these plains and parts. Perhaps there's some reason to continue living in this area, but it's been infected. There are ships that come from the sky that talk about the end days of Jalkdada QGF Ion, the multiverse that houses Zeffon, Earth, the Milky Way. If we consider Zeffon as a world of the mind, we can know for sure that it exists, but at the same time, it doesn't. It is a world that changes depending on the mind of the supreme individuals that come from the stars. Supreme is a loaded word, mostly because I believe that the masters of the multiverse are insane - they simply like to troll and mess with everyone they come across. This is exemplified in the time they let the dead loose from the Nacadja, the green temple east of Blueheart in the dimension of Zeffon. The question remains though: if Zeffon is a world of the mind, to whom does the mind belong?

Zeffon.title: I: Sol
Zeffon.about:
i. Marudescent
I: Sol is about the festivals that used to take place on the once-prosperous fourth continent.
ii. Ky
After the destruction of 2510, the leader controlling the region from a faraway land, the curse of the Arc-Demai was lifted, allowing the people of the town of Ghel to live as human beings once again.
iii. Rowta
The aforementioned festivals took place before those days, when the population had yet to turn to Arc-Demai.
iv. Meralansa
The legends say that the people were forced to build either a Suntower or a Moontower in order to cause the sun or moon respectively to rise.
v. Baracuthal
The land began to bear ill harvests and such when one of the towers was not completed in time.
vi. Temia-gerra
The festivals themselves mock the earlier times, and often take place around the ruins of the old Suntowers and Moontowers.
vii. Creek Funeral
In general, it's a time to not only celebrate being alive, but also communicate with the ancestors.
viii. Revamera
I: Sol represents the first part of this festival, which itself represents the proposal by the evil king Garimorg to his superior to create the tower ritual.
ix. Maeridetha
When the time came, it was time to do the best that the Yuuu could do. There was a battle ahead, and this one outclassed and absolutely diminished battles previous.
x. Shore
Something was up. Given the circumstances, it became clear that the upcoming Battle of Uya would be very hard and one-sided. There was nothing that could be done to remedy the situation that had begun to unfold.
xi. Yetamacanth
The statues below the battle (in a cavern with blind fish), exhibited a civilization that used to exist, its language long since lost.
xii. An Anthem For the Red Staircase
After the battle, many people were gone. Ratayu was spared the devastation, but the ancient ruins in the desert, along with the various nomads, had vanished from the face of the dimension completely. It was a terrible day for the world, and many people in Ratayu began to mourn. How could the curse of Zeffon carry over to the new dimension? What was causing it?
Trivia:
- Marudescent is meant to be a parody of Descent, one of the first tracks that appeared in the original Zeffon story.
- Ky stands for Yatsuhashi Kengyo.
- Creek Funeral is meant to be a parody of Sarah's Burial off of the album Generys Miasma.
- Maeridetha is a name derived from the name Meredith, an island in the Zeffon world.
- An Anthem For the Red Staircase is an improvised piece that was played on a keyboard into a tape recorder. It takes its name from various scenarios in the game Legend of Legaia.

Zeffon.title: II: Beware Anticipation
Zeffon.about:
i. Oakdash
They watch the stairs.
This album covers the story that the people of the Fourth Continent and Ghel conceived for the mystery of the continent of Exeräise. Legend has it that the last ancient king that used to rule over the continent demanded a sacrifice for the loss of his daughter. Thus, fugitives from an unknown location were locked in the Magot Tower, a massive stone brick tower built in the center of the large continent. The tower itself had torches on the top that could only be lit when the Bell of Noor (in possession of Exeräise at the time) was sounded. Now, according to the people of Ghel, the prisoners escaped because the kingdom abruptly collapsed that night. On the morrow, there was little more than little patches of grass amongst a mass of slate grey sand. Apparently, the prisoners escaped and found millions of worms on the ground with birds picking them off like crazy. According to the great Kin Tekraona, there was a sacred urn that the prisoners took back to their land that protected them that night and turned their captors to maggots that were then picked off by the morning birds. What the urn is however still remains a mystery.
ii. The Choice
The number is vermilion, one block for eyes. Can they stop the scorched earth?
iii. Marksmen
Reve Isga was the only one without a killing name. Why did the Third Eye curse our children of Unkardia? They were the only ones who were not allowed to continue to Ratayu.
iv. Kelmantha
According to what I've heard, we must stop Caria moving through the prophetic dreams. That's according to what the prophets have said.
v. 76: Island of Sanity, Wind Book
The Wind Book is written by a person seen by the first Hari.
- Trivia:
- 76: Island of Sanity, Wind Book is the last of the books that occur in the Number Series. The Number Series itself is a arrangement of ninety songs that remains incomplete as of May 13, 2014. It probably will never be finished. The Wind Book itself, as opposed to the other elemental books, represents humanity's ascension away from sorrow.

Zeffon.title: III
Zeffon.about:
And then I died...
Created mid-October 2013. The track "Median" was featured on the EP "Kelué". The tracks "Kelué, Pt. 1", "Kelué, Pt. 2". and "Chaosfoundry II" were all featured on the track "Ghost Memories" on the album Chaosfoundry II.
~
The EP "III" is about the ruins of the Uaa. The colossal town that once existed in the Aura Region disappeared a while ago, as a catastrophic landslide took the coastal ruins into the sea. These ruins have never been explored due to regional wars and a lack of technology. The Seraph Territories have claimed ownership over the ruins along with the Sharhodeon Territories and Icrifeani. The album itself is a radio transmission that was picked up by the Seraph Territories, coming from the ruins itself.
~
i. Birthday
I understood that the way to the castle was something that I did not understand. I didn't realize that I was ready to meet the man behind all of Zeffon's tragedies however.
ii. Moontower
The next battle of Ooogthe took place in this time. I was fascinated by the sheer will of the people of Eresymcaion, the ones that still wanted to fight. Nothing could have prepared me for their sheer audacity of hope.
iii. Befraelanthe
I knew there was nothing I could do. As I entered the ruins, the men of the age stood around and looked at me silently, as if judging me with their vacant eyes and expressions. What could I do?
iv. Plains of Doubt
The next battle of Yyyraao took place in the autumn. The old king began to fall and the new people began to arise from the ashes of their tarnished kingdom.
v. Median
I knew for the split second that I was around the men of the covenant that there was a problem. These men didn't seem to believe in their master, the almighty Jakioioogahna. I decided that it was time to speak in a way that I hadn't for millennia.
vi. Soul Eater
The yellow and green souls where the only ones that seemed to understand my ancient words. The red souls seemed confused, and the grey ones just scared. After I began the second part of my speech, they began to cheer.
vii. Kelué, Pt. 1
Kelué!! Coriario!! Meerrahhhh cetk to daaarrrstram oooraggah to teeeia slee oru meneraiii, Hasta mere graiwwhain!! These are the words that I spoke that began to cause a rise in their consciousness and began to cause them to want to fight for their master.
viii. Kelué, Pt. 2
Their master Jakioioogahna was most pleased. Being the third being besides Muagarah and Eresymcaion, he knew that his existence had a purpose. Forward, he said. We will understand and destroy anything that proposes to stand in our way.
ix. Chaosfoundry II
I understand the idea of THEE-PHERENTH, the idea of PAN-II, THY-II, and MONIUM-II, and thus begins my new journey!
x. The Morrow (Listening to the Grass Grow)
Until the morrow and a red and new dawn, I shall be asleep, said Uryetyaaaja. We shall conquer!

Zeffon.title: Ijumadasce
Zeffon.about:
i. Burning
A strange aura fills the air. One filled with nightmares and plague. The recent course of events filled Roanin with fear. He knew that he had to get to a shelter quickly. The sun was going down, and Roanin didn't want to be caught in the dark on the Great Marsh, for roaming the lands at night boded ill for past souls. Such was the case of Ulysses Paragi, who was sucked into the mire following Dr. Uy's trip elsewhere. Following a recent letter that Rowland received, he wanted to find a man named Thorn. Thorn Ansede to be exact. Apparently it wasn't just Dränsilane Isga that penned the Disynxiym. He had an accomplice.
-
Caria woke up. She felt groggy, and was confused as to what was going on. She began to remember the dream that she had when she suddenly fell asleep. There was a strange dimension filled with floating rocks that moved in waves like the ocean. She struggled to stay on top, but then slipped and tumbled into the darkness below. There was a loud crash, and then she opened her eyes. The sound of frogs began to bleed into Caria's consciousness, and she became fully aware that she was in fact not dreaming.
ii. Nerve Gas
A song dedicated to the ancients of Unkardia.
There was another sound, some sort of hiss. Caria covered her ears instinctively, until she realized it was not one of the stone snakes. A strange odor drifted into her nostrils, and Caria began to hallucinate. Suddenly, the area around her was black, but she was still able to move. Upon seeing light off in the distance, she approached it, wondering what it was. As she walked, she eventually come across a blazing fire as the source of the light. She heard a sound from behind her, and she turned around, discovering that there was a strange armless being that stood behind her, a face of pure terror on its head.
iii. Time of the Summoning, Pt. 1
The sun went down, casting shadows until they were farther than the eye could see. Anticipating a horrible roar in the distance, Roanin continued quickly, trying to make progress. Rowland mentioned that the cause of the death of Roanin's parents may be contained within the Disynxiym, or at least some clue. According to Dränsilane's writings, Roanin was born to a man named Rowland and a woman named Ophela, though Roanin could not remember those names at all.
Caria woke up for the second time. She, knowing full well that there was something around the Ognian ruins trying to manipulate her, sped out of the area as quickly as she could. She had heard of the legends of what happened when one's personality split, and she wanted no part in it.
iv. Manuscript 13
Roanin made it to the cabin, where Rowland was waiting.
"You made it, sir."
"Yes." Roanin panted slightly, having run the last quarter-mile or so. It appeared that Rowland had a book on the table. Scribbled on the open page was the following:
On this day, RTL was born.
On this day, RTL died.
And though she passed away long ago.
It is a mere husk that continues to live.
And with this final writing,
It is I, Thorn Ansede, the author of our story thus far,
Who will pass away as well.
May my words be interpreted as metaphor
And not fact.
"Is that the Disynxiym?" asked Roanin.
"It is indeed. I don't quite remember this passage being here." Rowland flipped through a couple more pages. "Is that the longbow?"
Roanin handed Rowland the mysterious object. Covered in vines and moss, it didn't seem like an object that Dränsilane would've used recently.
"Wow. I didn't quite expect it to be in this bad of shape. But you see those letters there?" said Rowland, thumbing some carvings in the rotten wood. "Those are Unkardian runes. Plus, this looks to be quite old."
"So if Dränsilane used this ancient bow, it must mean that he is from the past?" Roanin paced slightly, trying to understand. "Can you travel through time?"
"I don't know," said Rowland. "I just know that there's something incredibly odd about how this book seems to keep writing itself."
~
Caria eventually made it to a small village by nightfall. The townsfolk greeted her warmly, but she felt that they had other intentions.
v. Ritual 0
A harvest does not need to be one of maize or wheat...
Or so it is said. Reve Terra Lyeon contemplated what the word "harvest" meant for the continent of Unkardia. She began to use her psychic powers to unravel the mysteries kept within the Dragon. Surely he would oblige, as he had nothing better to do than to act as the bringer of doomsday, patiently waiting for the opportunity, or permission, to strike Zeffon and other worlds with his malice. The room began to hum and resonate as Reve concentrated harder and harder. Then, she got the answer she was looking for.
HARVEST IS A KEYWORD FOR A CIPHER. THAT CIPHER IS AS FOLLOWS:
HARVESTBCDFGIJKLMNOPQUWXYZ.
DO WITH IT WHAT YOU WILL.
vi. House of Skulls
Though he may be an emotionless experiment conceived at the hands of a genius, he was still very good at the piano and the trumpet...
Caria suddenly felt odd, like there was some sort of worm making its way through the ground below her, as the ground was starting to pulsate, as if it were alive.
vii. Ijumadasce
Thus was the self-titled Dr. Uy, a spawn of a horrible experiment. However, it was unknown to many that Derek Unmattias was perhaps the most human of all the creatures on the Earth. "Humans" became part of a special species a long time ago, hence the wording of some of Dränsilane Isga's poems. Despite being translated from Unkardian by Dränsilane's accomplice and scribe, Thron Ansede, they turned out fairly accurately, though in accordance to Dränsilane's wishes, parts of the poem were encoded with a simple cipher:
Farewell my green Earth.
I remember the day...
…Pbkqtb we hne oqagcie
Wene ucrpcio pk pcie…
...Pbe vhy, pbe oqj.
C neieiaen pbei wegg...
...The day, the sun.
I remember them well...
Pbnkqtb pbe uhnckqo gceo...
...Oqllkoe kje vhy C rkie.
Hjv C anehf pbe olegg.
Kb, bkw C neieiaen pbe vhy...
...Suppose one day I come.
And I break the spell.
Oh, how I remember the day...
Kjre we wene skqjv
We fjew we wene akqjv
Kb, bkw C neieiaen pbe agkkvy vhy...
...And the ghastly odor
Of your inevitable decay.
Hjv pbej kqn ejeiy vceo...
Pbnkqtb behuy netnep we wcgg rkie pk penio
Hjv pbnkqtb h ophge, mqcrfhntynkocqi
We obhgg rehoe pk wncpbe ho wknio.
A huge explosion occurred outside of the house that Caria was in.
viii. Comprehnsn.66
Then, existence
Though thoroughly complex
Is still only comprehensible
Forever shall we exist
On the lunar plane
For we are the worms
And the enemy is the crane.
~~
