This one was the former Trahma of the Groooalaahh clan (the leader). The Trahma began to experiment, coming up with a way to tap into the Lunar Plane from Ratayu and thus become a god.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.lyrics: xii. #0_800003051757813 The Battle of Yteia began to take place as this Trahma began to rise from the ground and take on the two warring gods, as well as the Third Eye. Not all was right with the world, and soon it became obvious that something needed to be done.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: Greed
trackinfo.lyrics: xiii. Greed A young girl by the name of Caria, the only daughter of a woman named Madeline Crowa appeared in the town one day, after a portal opened and just as quickly closed, depositing Caria in the town square. She was nursed back to health and when she realized that there were still problems occurring between Eresymcaion and Muagarah (albeit with new gods in the mix), she became contemplative, trying to figure out how to stop the four powers from warring.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: Reverse
trackinfo.lyrics: xiv. Reverse The essence of Dream VIII, or the eighth dream began to wander around the town of Ratayu, looking for a vessel to spread its message. It found Caria.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: Terraformed Fortress of Winds
trackinfo.lyrics: xv. Terraformed Fortress of Winds The first dream (Dream I) occurred when the people of Ocsania began to have nightmares and moved to Viandor across the sea. Ever since, the people of Zeffon in various stages and dimensions have made it their duty to seek out additional dreams. Dream VIII, or the eighth dream began to become a very apparent vision for Caria, and she saw a strange swampy land filled with ancient statues and the like, as well as a fortress that could house the likes of the gods.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: A Cursed Avenger of Sorts
trackinfo.lyrics: xvi. A Cursed Avenger of Sorts It became clear of the Battle of Gagrhe that there was a fifth god coming into play. Eresymcaion knew that its battle had been lost, and thus retreated into the ancient ruins beyond the desert, perhaps to never be seen again.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: Scales
trackinfo.lyrics: xvii. Scales Vald was the name of the fifth god, who came into existence from across the sea. He brought his followers with him and decimated the old Temple of Muagarah, causing Muagarah to become wrathful. It became clear that there was no hope for the Vald as Muagarah descended upon him.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: A Path to the Vacant Dream
trackinfo.lyrics: xviii. A Path to the Vacant Dream The strange battle of Yuuuggureaooooh occurs during this time. At this point, the administration has gone crazy searching for the eighth dream, as they haven't realized that it has been Caria who has had it.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: The Stranger With A Lamp
trackinfo.lyrics: xix. The Stranger With A Lamp The stranger who originally moved Zeffon to its second phase appears in the middle of the town square in Ratayu, causing a very loud ruckus that causes many civilians to dash to the square to see what's going on.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

trackinfo.title: 11: Unwelcome Dwellers, Water Book
trackinfo.lyrics: xx. 11: Unwelcome Dwellers, Water Book The stranger leaves behind a very specific clue addressed to Caria: do not drink the water in the pyramid, regardless of what you do. It is poison.
trackinfo.credits: from Stone Man, released April 7, 2014

Zeffon.title: Stormbringer
Zeffon.about:
i. Melody of Unknown Significance
This album is meant to be sort of a pseudo-live album and represent a performance. In a more curious line of research, the Kingdom of Lavu finally unearth the original "Serenade for the Dead" composition, by a long-since dead musician who has never been named. Given that the composition is considered a fundamental piece of Lavu's history, all six movements are quickly scheduled to take place at the Opera House in Blueheart, with even the Supreme Leadership in attendance. After the orchestra warms up, the first three pieces are played. Midway through the performance, the Supreme Leadership attendees leave. Samuel Cathrop has reportedly been captured. After a brief pause, the orchestra picks up where it left off and plays the remaining three parts. Strangely enough, the rain from outside begins to become increasingly audible through the opera house walls...
Movement descriptions - (Serenade for the Dead was written in the context of a story.)
I: Stormbringer - A simple pizzicato piece, meant to be used as an intro. Demons rise from the ground to destroy humanity.
II: Psychosis - Erratic percussion represents humanity's fear, as well as the inability to resist temptation.
III: Serenade For The Dead - A doomy piece meant to represent humanity's desperation for the wisdom of those passed away.
IV: Stone Face - Humanity is blessed with courage, and does away with their cowardice.
V: Perpetual Autumn - Time begins to stop for the decaying Earth. The living reunite with their dead loved ones. The ocarina in this track represents both the living and the dead ascending to heaven to be together forever.
VI: Goetia - The demons fade away as the Earth is left behind for a better world beyond.
Creator had known about our plans for a while after we had set them in stone as our life-long goals. We knew this when Keshka disappeared. He had been locked away in prison, but we didn’t realize that at the time. Meanwhile, a melody that Creator had been searching for came into the public eye for the first time.
ii. Opera Blueheart
According to history, Creator, when he was known as Harris, visited Unknown Iahae in the Temple of the Sun. Harris was the only person that Unknown Iahae would willingly talk to, and the two decided to collaborate on an ancient melody, which would be recorded on phonoautographs.. It was only years and years later that Creator revealed its location. With the modern technology he possessed, Creator deciphered the phonoautographs into sheet music that could be read by an orchestra, in five separate parts. Me and Emeroch were invited to appear at the first showing of the Serenade for the Dead at Opera House in Blueheart. We both could smell a rat, what with Keshka’s disappearance, but we decided to play with death and accept the invitation. Upon our arrival, the orchestra warmed up in the strangest of ways. We thought for sure that they would all whip out guns and start shooting us in the front row. Fortunately, this did not happen. Then the performance began.
iii. I: Stormbringer
The first part was supposedly a reference to a previous apocalypse following the arrival of demonic creatures on Earth. We could sense something odd as well, since a thunderstorm was brewing outside the hall, and different birds and frogs were becoming increasingly audible through the opera house walls.
iv. II: Psychosis (Stormbringer Outro)
The piece ended with an outroduction featuring nothing but percussion. This piece supposedly represented humanity’s inability to resist temptations and reflected their fear as well. The piece, though long, amplified the strange feeling I was experiencing. Apparently, this piece serves as a “spirit cleanser”, preventing interference from outside forces following its duration.
v. III: Serenade For The Dead
The main event occurred during this segment. This was the self-titled segment called Serenade For The Dead, which represented the wisdom of those that was desperately needed to defeat the demons that had invaded Earth, but had disappeared with the death of humanity’s ancestors and elders. The Rowland Meylith entered to view the performance, but soon left after he received a message from a boy who entered shortly after. According to what I overheard, Samuel Cathrop had been captured. In response, Rowland and his guards quickly left, causing some uneasiness in the crowd and the orchestra. After the Serenade was complete, the orchestra took a break.
vi. Gondii Maledicta, Pt. 3
We decided to leave at that point. Though the orchestra would pick up where it left off, we had better things to do, other than wait around for some assassin to try and kill us. With Rowland out of the opera house, we were free to go as we pleased. In my mind, I couldn’t help but feel that someone to whom I was very close was in danger.
vii. Cosmos
You could not see the stars through the unusually heavy clouds, but something unusual was returning. Something I had not seen for a long time.
viii. Dark Comet, Pt. 2
The Dark Comet was back. Its presence could only mean the next breed of dominant species was about to be chosen. The Dark Comet had only come three times in the past, but each time, it had caused for a new species to be dominant over every other kind. Since humans were the dominant species on Earth currently, I had a horrible feeling about this.
ix. IV: Stone Face
As I may have mentioned before, I honed my Instinct excessively when under the influence of Ryan. I was close to becoming perfect when I stopped myself. You see, if one hones their Instinct until it becomes flawless, their instinct develops a mind of its own in individuals with Dark in their blood. The clone then splits itself from its master and takes on the form of the person whom it used to serve.
~
Bqihjcpy co ageooev wcpb rkqnhte, hjv vkeo hwhy wcpb pbecn rkwhnvcre.
x. V: Perpetual Autumn
This Instinct then becomes indestructible. Though I’m not sure, it’s possible that the Serenade for the Dead references people who came across this dilemma, people who were so obsessed with their own power, that they could not prevent themselves from honing their Instinct and killing themselves off as a result. According to what I’ve read, the final part of the Serenade for the Dead represents the arrival of Archer Revenge, the human who would restore order.
~

xi. VI: Goetia

xii. Chaosdrive
Later on, I found out that Samuel Cathrop had been terminated using a specimen of Gondii Maledicta…

Zeffon.title: Stuka-food
Zeffon.about:
>The title and part of the music is based on a fake news story that the microwave oven is to be feared due to the effect of its radiation on the human body - and that the Nazis invented it. Thus, Stuka-food. Basically, I've taken a silly idea passed as fact and created silly music that seems like it should be taken seriously. Aside from this, the story I write with Zeffon continues, as usual.
i. No Strength to Stand
In the end, I came across a strange dimension and wrote about it in my journals, which I published. There's no doubt in my mind that they inspired Rufus Maye to begin writing his own pieces. In any case, I began to hear voices and music while in that forest, and soon, I saw light for the first time in years, as the forest is very dense. Eventually, I managed to walk a distance across what appeared to be a wheat field covered in sand. In the distance, I was able to make out clouds of dust erupting from the ground, telling me that I was going to have to make it past some sandstorms of all things.
ii. Mining Accident
After traveling farther, what used to be a wheat field began to look like a desert; there was nothing but sand dunes as far as the eye could see. All the while, I heard rumbling beneath my feet, which hit me with a sense of unease for no reason I could discern. I managed to make it to a small town, which the folk nearby called Kelios. They seemed surprised that they had received a visitor, as they had not seen travelers in a long time. As such, they regarded me with suspicion.
iii. September Star
Nevertheless, they allowed me to stay in a run-down house that was still somehow standing. It belonged to one of the Ijleneph clan they said, but ever since she died, it had remained vacant. I had no idea who this person was, but I thanked them for their hospitality, albeit limited. As the sun drifted down past the horizon, there was the sound of guitar music in the night, as if there was some sort of gathering somewhere in the desert.
iv. Rotting Fruit Vials
After the night had passed, I set out again, but I would always seem to end back up at the town. The people of Kelios didn't seem surprised, and they would repeatedly offer me the same house that I had slept in initially. Having the need for shelter during the cold desert night, I didn't refuse. It was my fifth time sleeping in that house, and I could hear the usual guitar playing in the distance, but I felt as though there was something else out there. It reminded me of the feeling of when I would sense a person nearby (I was born a psychic), but I couldn't tell what this presence was. Nevertheless, I was intrigued, so I set out during the night, following this entity.
v. Yez, Part 1
I continued to walk over the sand, noting the rumbling beneath my feet had gotten slightly more intense. As I mentioned before, every so often, rumbling would occur underground, but I had gotten used to it by now. This time however, it was slightly more apparent then I remember. Luckily, a full moon lit the desert quite nicely, which drastically reduced the malevolent atmosphere that would've otherwise been present. The guitar was also louder, which I took as a sign suggesting that I might be close to what I was searching for.
vi. Yez, Part 2
As I continued, I saw strange twisted trees that had cropped up out of the sand, and I began to sense that the terrain was about to change again drastically. Soon, the humidity of the surroundings began to become a factor and my skin grew cold with condensation. I began to shiver, and a mountain of stone began to slowly manifest itself on the horizon as I continued to move towards it. Eventually, I reached the base of it and began to climb. I reached the top and looked down the other side, where I saw a valley that reminded me very much of Inejeheim: dreary, foggy, damp, forested, and cold.
vii. A White Bird Called
Suddenly, a loud hooting sound filled the damp air, and I shivered at the sound of it. A hole appeared in the dense fog in the valley, and I saw what appeared to be a lizard with very thin and long crane-like legs flopping about in the mud, as if it couldn't stand. The hooting sounded again, and the hole in the fog closed, followed by the most gruesome sound of bones being snapped in half.
viii. Taking Away Our Loved Ones
I ran back to Kelios, only to find it abandoned, and inside the house in which I stayed, I found a note:
"To the Man known who stayed here,
We have abandoned this town. IT has taken too many of our people, and we have decided that enough is enough. We have buried ourselves beneath the desert with our ancestors, and hopefully, we will see our families again, before that sadistic, lying THING tore them apart."
~ EI
As I finished the letter, the wind shifted, and I felt an ominous presence nearby. I hid under the covers of the bed I had used and waited until dawn, when the presence finally left.

Zeffon.title: Sugââr Taffy (Shorelines VIII)
Zeffon.about:
A turn of events would eventually lead to Oswel's demise, the friend of Morgan. Morgan had the unfortunate fate of having to look into the eyes of the man who cannot see, and thus no one would be able to recognize her - the effect of such black magic makes any personal connection made during the victim's lifetime unravel, and thus they are forgotten by anyone they know or once knew. However, shortly before Morgan's departure, Oswel received a warning from Joachim in a dream, a religious leader among several groups around the town of Kore-Ijra, and a spiritual leader among others: Morgan would come face to face with the nameless blind man known as Paskrerek (pass-ker-ek).
Joachim's visitation within that dream reminded Oswel of the tales his father Kelren spun about moving to the hamlet in which he now had a family of four. Upon suggesting the move to Shemgrama to make a better living, his father frowned. Sure, Oswel could potentially supply oi'em to Kore-Ijra, as it was a good herb needed in a lot of the local religious rites. However, there was the tale of Paskrerek, the former servant from Southlend-near-vermenion, who would often wander the area with that hex that was placed upon him years ago. Oswel might be in danger. Nevertheless, Kelren gave his blessing.

Zeffon.title: System No. 1
Zeffon.about:
i. Stretched Skin
These notes are records written about the old lab that exists in Briea. To provide an accurate record, these accounts are unmodified. You might find the accounts surprising.
~ Vari
Author I:
There is a strange lab near the edge of the lake near Briea. The town is old - very old - the roads are paved with cobblestone. There are ancient cathedrals here and there and many of the houses are clumped close together like stuffing. It's a lopsided, yet picture-perfect coastal city, and one would expect it to have that kind of reputation. Sadly, it does not. The buildings are halfway abandoned, and the power plant that generates electricity for the city's lights is abandoned as well. Refeaël used to be the biggest producer of new technology, even to the point of its own demise. With the desire for knowledge came the desire to remove any sort of barricade that would otherwise obstruct this flow of power. In Briea, the traditional buildings are the main buildings left standing, but there is still that lab that is in business. In general, there are strange people who wander towards the lab. They come back, but they always bear a face of fear and wonder upon their return, as if they are intrigued and equally traumatized.
ii. System No. 1 (A Broken Wheel of the Thread of Law)
One day, a man was found shot in the streets. There was little sign of a struggle, and many people assumed that he had committed suicide. I remember I saw him lying there and decided to call to someone to pick up the corpse - I certainly wasn't doing it. It was nearly a week before someone journeyed down to Rey Street where I lived with a shovel and tossed the corpse in a nearby alley. Normally, this sort of treatment for the dead would shock people, but not after what we'd been through.
A few years ago, a tall man visited Briea. He was accompanied by a smaller man nearly a fifth of his size. Both men seemed to ignore the ongoing ruckus in the filthy streets and proceeded to continue in the direction of a certain apartment that we on Rey Street dreaded passing by. In general, the apartment itself looked perfectly okay from the outside. However, one of the young boys was watching the suspicious house from afar on a dare. A well-dressed man with a limp slowly shuffled up to the door and rang the doorbell. The chime rang, and about 3 seconds later, there was a terrible screeching noise, like someone was taking a knife to a small animal. The boy screamed loudly and hid. The next day, the boy still hadn't returned home.
iii. The Law
It was after this event that people started avoiding the apartment at all costs. The boy remained missing until the local police became motivated enough to be involved. Soon, a couple of "MISSING" fliers were pasted on a few different walls. It was when the last fliers were being put up that the police station received a wooden box on their front steps. It was found because it rang loudly in a metallic fashion whenever it was dropped - the person who dropped it on their front step likely had trouble transporting it.
iv. So Safe Flying...
I saw them open it. Out came a strange metal object wrapped in springs. While it looked like a piece of a larger contraption, I watched from a distance. I knew that there were some people out there who did not like the people in charge of Briea, since the boy going missing was not an isolated event.
v. Temporary System No. 1
In the days of old, there was nothing but dense evergreen forest where Briea is located. Briea was built by the New Refeaëlese Government during an industrial golden age over 2000 years ago. Supposedly, the forest was a resting place for many undead, but this didn't stop the individuals from cutting down the trees and making the large city. Eventually, problems started to arise. There was one of the first buildings that was created for Briea that suddenly burst into flames and set the Old District of Briea ablaze. People then report seeing two men walk out of the inferno, take the a small girl, and carry her back into the flames.
vi. System No. 2
Author II:
There's still something odd about that lab though. That's apparently where they do experiments on people they consider "unfit for a social means". At least, that's what the propaganda posters say. Other posters I've seen have nothing but collages of faces and heads on them. Usually they say things like "Forward!", but one poster for the lab struck me as odd. It was a collage of purple stone statues (just the heads), sliced through the nose as if the head was composed of two halves. It's almost like they're trying to get us to think of something so they can experiment on us later. It's quite strange to be honest.
vii. System No. 3
A tragedy has befallen the town of Briea. I recommend to my relatives, loved ones, or whomever to avoid the town like the plague. We're here, but we cannot get out. We are trapped. We cannot get out.
viii. Dimension of Omnivores
Apparently, strange people come out of the lab when the machines turn off. They look like regular individuals, but we can't help but believe that they're different somehow. It's really quite scary. We believe we've done anything and everything in our power to protect our town from these beasts, but we've been intimidated into staying quiet. No longer.
My friends claim that they've had children taken from them in the dark of night. Also, older men claim that they've woken up with a hunchbacked man sticking probes into holes in their head. When these men get up, there's nothing unusual going on at all, so they assume that they're hallucinating. However, many people claim to have experienced the exact same thing, lending some credibility to this "hallucination". Some believe that the experiments are aimed at re-implementing the old tribal cannibalistic culture of Refeaël. Yes, we used to be people who would kill anyone who used to come into our lands, but that was 2000 years ago. Why would we want to repeat that? The answer? A cloaked man told me it was more for fun, or "jest".
ix. M79
To experience a revival of the old tribal ways of Refeaël sounded so absurd, that I literally laughed in the man's face. He simply looked at me as if dumbfounded by my response. Apparently. the movement was bigger than I originally anticipated. That was the reason for the purple head poster that I saw plastered onto a decaying building wall. It was true. The old ways were returning.
x. Boil Water
Author III:
I encountered a small building on my travels. It looked fairly modern. It was as though it had just been freshly built, as all the surrounding structures were muddy and in desperate need of repairs. A child gestured me inside, and I felt compelled to follow. When I came up close to the person, I realized that it was not a child at all, but a man of about 3 feet in height. He asked me something in an unintelligible accent, and I could do nothing be shrug. He seemed greatly saddened by this and closed the door. I stood out in the rain, unsure what to make of the encounter. I had just decided to move towards the town of Briea, when the door opened again and the man gestured, guiding me inside.
xi. Death in the River
The inside of the house was covered not in experiments as I had heard the townsfolk go on about, but in letters, sweet smelling flowers that appeared to be freshly picked, and wooden chairs. The small man beckoned me to sit in a chair and wrote a note to me on one of the papers that was left lying about.
"You heard about the death in the river, correct?"
I wrote back.
"No, I have not. Who died?"
"My son, Lloyd."
"I'm very sorry. My condolences."
Just then, a small girl ran into the room.
"Daddy!"
The dad and the young girl who appeared to be about five years old were approximately the same size. The dad remained silent.
"Who's this, Daddy?"
The dad remained silent still, tears welling up in his eyes. I began to assume that the father could not speak due to some ailment or other. The father seemed to read my thoughts, and with that, he handed me a note that had been pre-written.
"Hello Vaughn,
You may not have expected to come here, but I knew that you would. I am in hiding due to charges that were brought against me in my home country. I am innocent, but a being of the unknown continues to taunt me and control people in such a way that it causes me to suffer. I have lost the ability to speak, but I need your help nevertheless. Please hear my plea. I need you to help protect my daughter Emilie, as the unknown has already taken my son."
xii. Temporary System No. 2
The unknown apparently set the town of Briea on fire, according to the man. That's why the building he was living in looked so much fresher - he had protected it from the flames. As I journeyed on, I saw the old buildings of what seemed to have been an ancient, yet industrial town. Human bones littered the empty streets, and every so often, a rat would scamper across the wet road.
xiii. Death Evening
I found a few men wandering the old town after a while. They said that they had come to visit friends and family many years ago, and that they found nothing but ruin. They also seemed to agree that whatever ravaged Briea was some sort of unknown beast, something that could not be seen nor heard from. I asked them how that worked, and they shuddered. It was as if the town was okay one second, and in enormous flames the next.
"The unknown has no time-frame," said one man, "It just is. Whatever it wills comes to be."
xiv. M69
A strange noise filled the air, and I knew it was time to get going. It sounded like a strange clicking noise, like someone or something popping its tongue in some sort of fashion, as if to beckon me away from the group like some sort of animal. I fled Briea that night, and never visited it again. I knew there were forces that I must stay away from, and I decided to do so.
xv. Infestation in Lung
According to what I know, these roads still remain untraveled. I don't blame any sort of individual who refuses to venture towards Briea, or Refeaël for that matter. I remember before I eventually left the country, I was stopped by cloaked woman.
"Who are you?" she hissed.
I refused to say my name, and she grabbed me and slammed me into the ground.
"You've seen him!"
I didn't know what she was talking about. I thought of the small man who lived in the only standing house in Briea, and dread flooded my mind. Suddenly, the woman looked up and fled into the darkness of the night. I have no idea what she saw, and I decided not to look behind me to find out. I kept fleeing down the road and didn't stop until I saw the sun.
xvi. Smashed Cicada Shells
Author IV:
I decided after a bit of contemplation that I should head to the country of Jama. It was in the Center of the Chaoslands, and it seemed to connect with the tragedy that befell Briea. I am a detective after all. I traveled from Windor in the Seraph Territories and eventually arrived in the city of Wreath. All the cities out here are city-states in the sense that there are no true borders dictating boundaries. Jama is the official name of the city-state that contains the city of Wreath. It is a large city, one that Lavu did not feel the need to take over. In any case, I decided to look at an anonymous tip that I got that the country of Jama had something to do with the burning of Briea. I eventually met the man who I was looking for. His name was Oscar. Apparently, he had been through a lot and had come to Wreath to settle down and retire. He had a strange museum of objects he said he'd like to show me.

Zeffon.title: Tape 8
Zeffon.about:
i. Limbo (Extract)
I'm not sure what to make of the new town that cropped up. There's an old factory that has had a town built around it, and it's very odd, considering no one's let into the town without a special pass. I live in Verimore, but I've never seen anything like this in my lifetime. The town's name is Wracon.
ii. Space Patrol, Part 2
Wracon is a closed town in the sense that it has nothing available to the general public. Yet, there's a factory always producing something while I pass the town on the road. Smoke would rise high and pollute the horizon until the entire sky became a vibrant red-orange.
iii. Horror Scene From a Film
Filmakers have hypothesized about Wracon for the longest time. Someone managed to make it inside at one point, procuring a cassette tape from the factory's inner workings. The audio found on the tape has been published here.
iv. Dimensional Rift (Extract)
According to people I've talked to, the tape has a lot of connections to the Wje, a people who used to populate a place on the alternative world - also the Hehe. I have no idea what this is supposed to mean, except that there was a revival of a certain individual that meant to do the alternative world harm.
v. X-Ray Block Machine Phantom
In any case, the tape went missing after I duplicated the audio. In a world like Zeffon, anything like that can happen. I'm hoping that hopefully I'll be able to be privy to more of the stuff that's happening beyond the veil.
Revival.
In a world where Muagarah's energy reigns supreme, it's very interesting to see that there are people who develop a sense of the creative. In a sense, the darkness is good for us all, as it really set the mood for artists and musicians alike to be creative in cities like Whip and Wracon. We as an artistic group called XRTH have managed to find a way out of Zeffon, through the creation of art. It is an anthem for the mighty in psychic-ry.
vi. Mining Town (Extract)
Revival.
Revival.
Revival.

Zeffon.title: Temple of the Sun
Zeffon.about:
i. Unknown Iahae
Temple of the Sun occurs during the end of Unknown Iahae's lifetime. The Temple of the Sun itself is a sanctuary of light in comparison to the rest of the world, which is shrouded in dark clouds. When Unknown Iahae is rediscovered by the priests of the Temple of the Sun, he is commissioned to protect the sanctuary by creating a mystical spell with his music. Unknown Iahae knows this will not work, and would rather live as hermit for the rest of his life, instead of deceiving the entire human race for years to come. The head priest however, insists. Unknown Iahae is arrested and brought before the head priest, and told to write a Serenade that will grant the temple immunity against those who wish to destroy it. Left with little choice, Unknown Iahae writes the Serenade for the Dead on phonautographs, making them impossible to interpret, and then escapes the temple with Movement 9. An arrest warrant is issued, but Unknown Iahae has disappeared entirely. Soon after, an ancient foe destroys the heavily guarded temple from within, and the Holy Stone Age Order collapses.
ii. IX: Oasis
It is mysterious who Unknown Iahae actually is. But the mysterious powers present in everything seem to display the true nature of his existence. My name is Drai Fair Onh, a descendant of Fair Onrac and his mother, Igen. This means a lot to my existence really, since I'm related to someone so obviously evil, and yet no one knows why. My ancestor just had a connection with the powers of the unknown, shall we say. He was very versatile in this knowledge, and he knew a lot of different things. Due to this, he got lost in what is only known as the Eternal Wood. He went searching for the ghost man known as Unknown Iahae and he disappeared in that cursed forest without a trace.
iii. Timeless Death
It is said the only thing that remains of him is the Wooden Mask that he would wear to summon demons. Many people don't know what this mask is, but I do. It's the culmination of his years of research.
iv. Holy Stone Age Order
You see, my ancestor found that there's a certain power that rises with the idea of being unknown. Basically, the less known someone is, the more power they have against people of the opposite side of the spectrum. Although my ancestor is famous by name, no one really knows much about him except me. This gives him his mystic power. However, even though it is said that individuals that are not well documented and even unknown are dreadfully powerful in power, this power diminishes by becoming known to other people, in an exponential fashion shall we say. If a man can move mountains with his hand, if someone realizes this, he may only move boulders, being reduced to gravel and dust over the episodes of other peoples' realizations.
v. Mist Serpent
My ancestor sought to control this, and this he did well. While unknown, he evoked a nameless dark power that shall be nameless for all eternity due to its strength. It's sheer fortitude means that it cannot be named, and can only refer to itself as "I". The Great I created a giant beast and placed under the earth. The Unknown Beast drains the willpower and stamina of those who come near it, much like the scattered pieces of Castle Adelais, which bear the Unknown Beast's sign. There are three other creatures that do the bidding of the Unknown Beast: the decaying angel, the jackanapes, and of course, the mist serpent. These beasts are unstoppable as long as they have the power of the Great I.
vi. Curse The Land
The lands of anyone and everyone shall fall victim to this being eventually. The Unknown Beast is comprised of two warring gods, the Dark God Muagarah, and the Light God Eresymcaion. The component Light God is much weaker than its counterpart, and thus the world is doomed to drown in darkness - it's just a matter of time.
vii. Enemy Dies
I knew that writing this would cause me to become less powerful myself. Although I may sound evil based on how I write, I assure you, I have not a single drop of malevolence in my heart. Knowing the unknown contributes to odd effects on one's being, whether it be physical, emotional, or otherwise. Even as I write this, I am withering; I grow old. But don't worry - I shall complete this document before my time is up.
viii. Abyssal Forest
I shall tell everything I can muster. It is important and of the essence due to the nature of the I's effects on its surroundings. Even when I think about it, the I is probably controlled by an even stronger being, reaching out from a palm of an even stronger being, and so on, into the realms of infinity. Thus is I.
Zeffon.credits:
released February 5, 2013
Everything - Creighton Jenkins
Special Thanks to Aborted Existence (Printing and Tapes)

Zeffon.title: Tertiary Proteins 3
Zeffon.about:
Chalk Forest Mist of the Tyrns (Part 1 of 3)
(Told from the perspective of a philosopher writing in his journal, this is the story that accompanies the album/songs)
Because of the different dimensions within Z>, it becomes clear that there are parallels within every dimension, even ours. Our dimension (A>) is the one in which planet Earth is based.
Each of the dimensions (as far as I've observed and studied) MUST possess the following criteria to remain in existence. My apologies for the odd words; these are copied from an old tome. The requirements are as follows: ar-sem, öumi-pelmestat, pelmestat, handroteim, öumi-ar-adru, and ytrac-ar-oradru.
Chalk Forest Mist of the Tyrns (Part 2 of 3)
(Told from the perspective of a philosopher writing in his journal, this is the story that accompanies the album/songs)
According to the nameless tome I mentioned earlier, an Ar-sem, when it comes to dimensions, is necessary for a dimension to exist. Any sort of peacekeeper or creator will usually embrace this role.
An öumi-pelmestat is the challenger to the ar-sem's power.
A pelmestat (or pelmestats) are individuals caught in the middle of the fight between the ar-sem and the öumi-pelmestat. One might think of them as innocent civilians.
A handroteim is the öumi-pelmestat's designated assassin.
Öumi-ar-adru represents a dimension's state of peril. Once this peril has been resolved, the dimension will no longer exist, as öumi-ar-adru is required for a dimension's existence.
Ytrac-ar-oradru is the main philosophy behind the handroteim. If the handroteim loses interest in killing the öumi-pelmestat, the dimension disappears.
Another item of note is that a dimension can straddle the boundaries of traditional dimensions. For example, an event in Zeffon can affect an event on Earth.
Chalk Forest Mist of the Tyrns (Part 3 of 3)
According to the tome I found, handroteims usually lose sanity very quickly as they try to complete their lifelong task. As the name suggests, the individual who is the handroteim of his dimension is usually afflicted with a type of body rot that begins in the hands.
Handroteims typically have an awareness of what they are meant to do until their mind decays with the rest of their body. However, their mind never decays to the point of neglecting ytrac-ar-oradru - their goal.
In order for dimensions to exist properly, the handroteims must constantly be in pursuit of their victims: the öumi-pelmestat, and by that nature, the lowly pelmestats. The öumi-pelmestat is the leader of the civilian population, or pelmestats. Once the öumi-pelmestat is eliminated by the handroteim, the civilian leader becomes the next victim. The handroteim must be eternal, as, as mentioned before, a dimension cannot exist without its corresponding handroteim.
The Great Men of the Lord
According to the tome, this is a very rare 3rd Edition of Idil Madgod Hry Chyi. The first two editions were printed by Ui Mial, one of the legendary library publishers on the continent of Mödgod, dedicated to preserving history regardless how perverse. The Great Library of the Isle of Anne, founded by Adelais and Lydia Isga, is the only other library to rival some of the ancient ones that exist on Mödgod. Apparently, they still exist, but no one I know has been to Mödgod for years.
The 1st Edition of Idil Madgod Hry Chyi was published over 2000 years ago in the Marano Language, which is odd considering that Marano was not spoken by the civilian population of Inejeheim until about 1500 years later. Marano is an obscure minority language originating from the Isle of Daei. Swanish is and has been the main language for Daei Islanders since the beginning of time, but Marano was spoken as an even older language by a chosen few in the then fledgling town of Vahn. Vahn exists as a town within an extinct volcano, and was built there to withstand assualt from the outside. Given the small size of Daei, it's unclear what that assault would be from, but perhaps the shallows on the south western part of the island hold some clues. There are odd statues littered all about here, and appearently glow a brilliant neon purple under certain light.
In any case, Marano disappeared entirely from Daei, but somehow turned up in Inejeheim, spoken by a chosen few who were regarded as holy men.
The 2nd Edition of the tome was heavily revised from the 1st Edition, of which no legible copies are known to exist, as the massive low-temperature humidity of Mödgod has caused much of the ink in the last existing tomes to bleed throughout the pages. The 2nd Edition was heavily ammended, modified, and translated to Liia, a language that's supposedly spoken on Mödgod by a select few. Appearently, Idil Madgod Hry Chyi holds relevant information about the history of Zeffon that only people who understand Liia can comprehend. I seriously doubt it, but that's what's been said. The 2nd Edition has copies scattered throughout the globe.
The rare 3rd Edition disappeared entirely from different archives, as if the book was cursed. I myself had a very hard time trying to locate a copy. No more than 55 copies were originally printed. The 3rd Edition is an amended version of the 1st Edition, but the original text has been preserved. It comes in two languages: Marano and Kie. I have a Kie version, since Kie is a language that is spoken by commoners all throughout The Icrifeani and the Chaoslands in general. It's honestly exciting to have a slice of history this big in one's own personal library. Apparently, there's a story in this massive tome that was cut in the 2nd Edition, one I have yet to read. I'll provide an update when I find it.
I have often thought, now that I've read the tome and found out about handroteims, that Zeffon was a tad different from the rest.

trackinfo.title: Chalk Forest Mist of the Tyrns (Part 1 of 3)
trackinfo.lyrics: (Told from the perspective of a philosopher writing in his journal, this is the story that accompanies the album/songs) Because of the different dimensions within Z>, it becomes clear that there are parallels within every dimension, even ours. Our dimension (A>) is the one in which planet Earth is based. Each of the dimensions (as far as I've observed and studied) MUST possess the following criteria to remain in existence. My apologies for the odd words; these are copied from an old tome. The requirements are as follows: ar-sem, öumi-pelmestat, pelmestat, handroteim, öumi-ar-adru, and ytrac-ar-oradru.
trackinfo.credits: from Tertiary Proteins 3, released October 29, 2016

trackinfo.title: Chalk Forest of the Tyrns (Part 2 of 3)
trackinfo.lyrics: (Told from the perspective of a philosopher writing in his journal, this is the story that accompanies the album/songs) According to the nameless tome I mentioned earlier, an Ar-sem, when it comes to dimensions, is necessary for a dimension to exist. Any sort of peacekeeper or creator will usually embrace this role. An öumi-pelmestat is the challenger to the ar-sem's power. A pelmestat (or pelmestats) are individuals caught in the middle of the fight between the ar-sem and the öumi-pelmestat. One might think of them as innocent civilians. A handroteim is the öumi-pelmestat's designated assassin. Öumi-ar-adru represents a dimension's state of peril. Once this peril has been resolved, the dimension will no longer exist, as öumi-ar-adru is required for a dimension's existence. Ytrac-ar-oradru is the main philosophy behind the handroteim. If the handroteim loses interest in killing the öumi-pelmestat, the dimension disappears. Another item of note is that a dimension can straddle the boundaries of traditional dimensions. For example, an event in Zeffon can affect an event on Earth.
trackinfo.credits: from Tertiary Proteins 3, released October 29, 2016

Zeffon.title: ...The Demon Hunter Gets Trapped in the Evil Mist and Becomes a Worm
Zeffon.about:
i. Misery Does It
Something odd was frozen in the forest near the peak of Mount Yahahah. It was a person, probably the last person in the dimension of Zeffon (besides myself of course). I realized that this was the person that was preventing the complete collapse of the dimension itself, as it cannot exist with no people in it. This was the Creator's personage.
ii. The Asylum Song
The next battle of Yrhehh had occurred in Ratayu. Ratayu was on the verge of being overrun by the Third Eye's minions. The last thing standing in between the city and the armies of the Third Eye was the Great Wall. The Great Wall was built for this purpose, but it could only withstand so much abuse before it too was destroyed.
iii. Garden of Eden
Merrroaogggh was a man who was dying due to the Third Eye's spells. In the Castle of Keerreuuu, he became one of the Resistance. One had to be dead or dying to even think about resisting the Third Eye. One had to be stronger in death than in life, much like the Breath of Shadows who preceded them.
iv. Poisonous Snakes Fill the Cavity
Due to the Song of Curse, many people in the Castle of Keerreuuu will be walking as the living dead, their limbs rotten, their eyes glazed over. However, it is the sacrifice that they must make to destroy the Third Eye and his armies that produce chaos.
v. Worms
The desert worms have all disappeared, as something below the sand of the earth has begun to moan and shift, as if a giant creature of unfathomable size is underneath the desert having a nightmare.
vi. Precarious From the Sun
In the dimension of Zeffon, I knew that I didn't have the ability to make it to Ratayu, as the portal to that dimension had been closed and sealed a long time ago.
vii. Nar Releases Thousands
I went back to my house. There wasn't much to do as a lowly human in a dimension of beasts, ghosts, and undead. I did my best to make the best of it though. I thought in my mind about Caria, who managed to catch the portal to Ratayu. I had dreamed about her a couple of times since, and she had told me in my dreams about the dilemma in Ratayu. I honestly wished the best for her, but what was I to do? I was trapped.
viii. Misery
According to Caria, there was a town on the border that was frozen in permafrost. It was kind of hard to believe, especially considering the fact that Ratayu was in the middle of the New Chaoslands (a desert). There was an old prophecy written in the hills of Dotajmari, that the desert would freeze over at some point. According to Caria, the Dotajmari was a civilization that existed to the north of Lavu in the arid mountains. I've wondered what I could find there.
ix. Broken Ultraviolet Gas-Discharge Lamp
The interesting part about Dotajmari is that it was a strange place to be when there were more people in Zeffon besides myself. It had been the recipient of a calamity that no one could discern the origin of. It had been a victim of what many people (including myself) have refused to talk about for a very long time: the Sun. In my travels, I encountered a terrible thing folded into a wooden box. It had the appearance of a fetus with cuts all over it, as if it had been experimented on by some sort of religious cult. I became very frightened, as I knew that the Sun was using its power to intimidate me into submission. I knew a lot about the Dragon and the Sun by this point.
x. The Wind's Blood-chilling Scream
In the end, do not anger the Sun. The Sun has the power to shrink and destroy ANYONE. I recognized the poor shriveled creature, since I have psychic powers that allows me to read minds. The creature was once powerful, as the remnants of a few psychic abilities were still detectable near the corpse's head. This was someone who had been tortured and shrunk to a small size and then tortured some more. I realized that this creature was still alive.
xi. Poisonous Snakes Fill the Cavity
"Do not anger the Sun. Do not become an Enemy of the Sun," said the creature in its own mind. The words repeated endlessly through the psychic spectrum.
"What is your name?" I asked the creature.
"UAA," it said. "I was better known as Dränsilane." The creature opened its eyes, revealing nothing but eye sockets, dried blood caked on the inside. "Where am I?"
"You are in the hills of Dotajmari. You seem to have survived the wrath of the Sun, old king."
"Who is still alive?" asked the wretched creature.
"What do you mean?"
"Who from my family is still alive? The house of Isga?"
"All of them have been destroyed by the Sun, with the exception of one."
"Lydia," said Dränsilane with a fair amount of effort. "Lydia Isga, Reve Terra Lyeon, and Caria Crowa are still alive."
The ancient king coughed up blood. "My sister Reve did not deserve her fate. I don't understand what came over me when I last saw her, but I screamed at her for being weak. She died from an incurable illness."

Zeffon.title: The Excavation, Pt. 1
Zeffon.about:
The Excavation, Pt. 1
It is 1870. It is foretold that a man is born but is not given a name. Throughout his life, he wonders: Why was he abandoned so quickly at birth? His one artifact from his youth is a grossly carved figurine made of palm wood with a facial expression so grotesque, it fills the man with fear. With no answers to be had, the man blames a much older individual for his predicament, an elderly man with a crescent scar around his right eye, an eye he always keeps closed as if he’s winking. In the meantime, the man without a name ponders over the nickname given to him by the others in the orphanage: Father. As they grew older, they began to reconsider the name that they had given Father. Father was not a fatherly figure in any way. He was cold and unforgiving. By that time, it was too late, however. The name had stuck.
It is 1932. It is foretold that Father has grown up and had a son named Nathan with Charlotte, his wife. Being the “successful” man that he is, Father’s profits were lucrative, albeit not always legal. Oftentimes, Father came home with Vic and his men, Vic being the ringleader of the heists that they were committing at the time. Charlotte didn’t care at first, but grew increasingly defiant as Father talked about all the people they had shot but not killed. That was the thing that Father would emphasize. The victims were shot, not killed.
When Nathan’s Father has his second son with Charlotte, he thinks briefly of how deep he was into the robbery stuff that he did behind his wife’s back to keep her happy and rich. As it turns out, he is close to being Vic’s right-hand man by now. The last guy in this position didn’t take the job seriously enough and eventually “left”, opening the way for the post that was supposed be Father’s originally. All of the bank heists became quite a rewarding business for Father and Vic, and Father began to wonder if the police would ever upgrade their guns to something a little more “potent”.
It is 1933. It is foretold that Father has gained notoriety as a bank robber. Police were placed around where Vic and his crew would strike next. Shots rang out and caught the policemen by surprise. They had no chance at all of retaliating. The bank was robbed. Vic did not suffer any casualties. The police were all killed…
It is a year later. Things would have gone severely downhill by now. At this point, Charlotte will have had enough and leave Father following her discovery that his income was a bunch of “dirty money”. In order to support her lifestyle, she will run off with newborn Charlie and another rich man that wasn’t a “common thug”. Father would feel he’s innocent, but would have no way to prove it. “It was just to make you happy,” he would say. Of course, he would be talking to the empty house at that point. Charlotte will have already run away.
Father would leave Vic’s little operation following Charlotte’s departure and eventually convert to Christianity. Whatever he did, he would be sorry and want to beg for Charlotte’s forgiveness, though Charlotte will not give him any. She’ll say in a letter that Father was just another man, and the void that was left following his absence will easily be filled with someone else. She’ll admit she considered finally settling down when she married Father, but she’ll also say she had no intention of staying permanently in all honesty. However, despite Father’s inner turmoil, he would notice that the envelope was sealed in blood. After working with Vic all those years, he knew dried blood when he saw it. How terrible.
Nathan, who will be in his 20s at this point, will also disappear. A horribly distraught Father would just sit in his decaying mansion, weeping silently. One night however, Father gets a visitor. The moon looks colder than usual that night, a waxing crescent. Then father notices through the open window a man lurking around the yard. It’s him. It’s that man with the crescent scar around his eye, the eye that never opens. Father quickly stops sobbing and looks for his gun, but it’s not there. “Where’s my Thompson?” he mutters rather fearfully to himself. He looks back into the moonlit yard. There’s no one there. From that point until the next day, Father would not be able to remember anything.
Father would live in the mansion for the next few months, and notes the old, skinny, crescent-eye man in the dead yard every few nights or so. Unnerved, father would hide in the insane asylum far from where the mansion is, just so he could be left alone and die in peace. He would leave much of his acquired wealth behind, taking only an item that he had not seen for a long, long time: a sort of compass, borrowed by Nathan in his youth.
It is 1913. It is foretold that it will be another Wednesday when Nathan will have met with his friends in the park relatively close to the school that he would be going to. In the past, he will have felt the desire to borrow that one thing that his dad always treasured and show it to his childhood friend, an odd individual he called “Blank”. He will have had a fight with Father the other day and after things had supposedly simmered down, he will have made the decision to hold onto the compass, even if it was for a little while. He will not know why he had made that choice, but it will clearly be a mistake by that point. The compass will be gone. Blank will have taken it. Father would hit the roof. Unfortunately, when Nathan will finally get around to doing just that, Father would be anxiously rummaging through boxes of old coins and keys that he would have collected for no particular reason other than to have multiple boxes full of old coins and keys. When Father would finally hear the news, he would be furious at first, but then would just collapse on the couch, shaking his head.
“It wasn’t just a compass,” he would say. “It was a map in itself…” Nathan will just sit there silently, but will finally get the courage to speak.
“I can… I can buy you a new one,” he will stammer in an evident attempt to redeem himself.
"Nate, that’s not the point. I couldn’t give a rat’s hat over whether I have an old compass. I have all these other relics, so there would be no purpose to that.”
Nathan will smile, but still feel as though he will be the subject of some sort of hidden anger from his dad.
“Nate, do you remember how it had some symbols on it instead of things like North and South? It was a guide to that thing that your great-aunt had hidden on that island in the Pacific…”
Father’s visions would continue over the time spent at the asylum. They will not recognize him as a notorious bank robber and will commit him to the facility on the spot, thus achieving Father’s goal of avoiding the police and avoiding the crescent-eyed man. However, even throughout the months and years, father notices the creepy man wandering around the moonlit grounds outside of the sanctuary, as if he’s looking for something. Something unknown.
Nathan will already be heading towards the Pacific Island Father mentioned. It will be a very relaxed plane ride as he slowly works his way towards China. From there, Nathan will attempt to search the islands southeast of there. He will have received the compass he lost when he was a small kid in the mail. Blank will have mailed it to Father’s mansion with a note stating that the package must be opened by Nathan.
“Apologies,” the letter will say. “I didn’t mean to do the thing I did when you were a mere child. The compass that I stole from you all those years ago is now yours again. If you have the ability to act on your instincts, meet me in Shanghai, where we will depart to find your father’s treasure together and present it to him to get him out of the depressive state he’s in.
P.S. Don’t tell him about my twin brother.
Regards,
Blank.
Nathan will pull the compass out of his pocket and gaze upon it. The symbols in the place of letters had no significance to him, but he will be sure that Blank will fill him in. Suddenly, an explosion. The plane dips to the left as smoke and fire trails from engine number one. Passengers scream as the plane hurtles toward the ocean. Nathan will become sedated by the impact of the plane crashing into one of the few pieces of ground the pilot could find and will awaken with eyes searing, but will see absolutely nothing. Not only will the cabin be filled with smoke and fire, but he will be covered by the charred corpse of a fellow passenger, who had felt that it was his duty to protect the fainted boy on the ground from the imminent surge of flame. However, even after this act of heroism, the flames will grow hotter and Nathan will die, wondering if his dad will ever cope with the news of his demise. This is foretold.
At the thought of this, the already unstable mind of Father would lose all sense of reason. Thus, Father quickly corrected his thought process. Nathan was a good, capable young man. He wouldn’t die. He will not die. He would just faint again. He would be fine. He will realize if Father was in the same position, he would have died from inhaling all the smoke and embers…
Nathan will be dragged from the wreckage by another man. This man will drag him to a place where all the people go when they crash on that strange island. It will be called the House of the Lost. Here, Nathan will find that he had survived the flames and the trip to through the jungle without a scratch. Father would have gotten plenty of scratches. This is not foretold.
The people there will introduce themselves. There will be Clyde from the state of Texas, a curious man by the name of Ryan, plus the girl named Betty. Nathan will get up and shake hands with all of them since he sees them as responsible for saving his life. Eventually Nathan will help the people of the House of the Lost to move to a nearby island where they will find a strange little man while hunting for additional food and supplies. The little man will describe how he believes the world lives in a permanent lethargic age from which they cannot recover. Out of curiosity, the party will continue to speak the little man, who will eventually describe how he has been sitting in the jungle for years without food or water, and how everything around them is doomed to wither in the brightest sun, to become silent at the sight of their deepest fears, and once again, to succumb to the poisonous and lethargic miasma that had recently been introduced to the foul air. Nathan will think briefly of Father, one whom will still be incapable of breaking the chains around his mind and grasping reality through a thick veil of grief. Nathan would be able to escape an asylum. Father wouldn’t. Or would he? This is not foretold.
Nathan will eventually seek a way to escape the two islands that he and the people of the House of the Lost will be marooned on. The little man will have no advice at all; he’ll be focused on his meditation. No, the only answer would be ingrained in Nathan’s own ingenuity. Together, the foursome of the House of the Lost would build a boat, but they would be lacking a sense of direction. Nathan’s compass will be of no help, since the symbols will not correlate with the polarity of the Earth and the four directions on a map. With that in mind, the foursome will eventually give up, knowing it would be futile to rely on ocean currents to bring them across the Pacific Ocean. They will eventually find some solace in speaking to the little man, but Nathan will become agitated, determined to get off the island on way or another. Nathan will have that determination. Father wouldn’t.
Nathan will become separated from the party and come across a run-down mansion. He’ll think it probably once looked a lot like Father’s mansion, although it will be too small to be the same. In the mansion, he’ll find a lot of toys that he will swear he had when he was a kid. He’ll evidence that his Mother was here. Climbing the rotten steps, he’ll notice the faded pictures of Father and Mother. Not the man that Mother ran off with. The real Father. On an old writing desk, Nathan will find Charlotte’s letters to Father, and how she wished she could talk to him. However, the man that flew her to the island had no intention of reviving her relationship with Father, in case Charlotte ever found reason to return to the United States. There will be no signs of foul play. In fact, the letters that Mother wrote will seem to indicate that Charlotte’s husband had died within 5 years of their arrival, Charlie had disappeared, and that Charlotte was all alone.
Father began to ponder the thoughts that he had collected. Maybe the old man was right. Maybe Nathan is okay, even though no one knows where he is. Maybe I can manage to live the rest of my life without turmoil. Yet, there was Crescent-Eye. The thought of the old man always gazing upon his window disturbed him greatly. With that thought, Father quickly retreated back into his mind. Nathan was going to escape that island. He would have to.
Correction. It is 1939. It is foretold that a fire has started in the asylum. The doctors save themselves. Although many of the inmates find a way out, Father is trapped in his cell. Like the temperature around him, the temperature in the jungle will begin to grow hot…
Later, I found myself burning.

Zeffon.title: The Excavation, Pt. 2
Zeffon.about:
Part II of the Excavation. An old archeologist, amongst the first to find a Horrid Figurine, retires after witnessing the horrors brought on to the area nearby upon its discovery. This is his story.
Upon reaching the excavation site, there was a lot going on. People moving to and fro, people with wheelbarrows carrying material from the site that had been so callously blown up with dynamite. Little runes, once filled with information, were nothing but shards now. Some said it was not the nature of the men that had made them want to completely devastate the place that once held information on pre-Colombian society, but a mad sort of superstition that had destroyed the minds of these men for who knows how long.
The men told of a strange man who haunted their dreams. All of these men where present in fighting the fire that had destroyed an asylum on the edges of New York state. They had in fact applied for the excavation job just so they could destroy it; there was no doubt about that. Something had continued to haunt these men to the point of insanity. The archeologist didn't blame them, though. Despite the loss of the ruins, it had become apparent to him as well that some terrible things were best forgotten.
I had a friend named Blank; an odd name for sure. He had given himself this name in his childhood because he didn't appreciate his birth name. Although Blank knew that he had a genuine name and had a fascinating memory, he did not remember what his given name was or had ever been.
Recently, Blank had been reading odd letters that he had been getting in the mail (we were close enough that he would tell me about any happenings). The letters described a place beyond what he referred to as the "lunar plane". His correspondent was unknown; he didn't dare tell me his name. But Blank was clearly fascinated by the writings.
After I visited Blank following the 29th of November in 1915, he began to act as though he was not his usual self. He would write letters addressed to odd locations that did not amuse the local post office. At first, I thought it was a prank. He would often write to places called things like Varii-Gree, Tomhet, and Oasis. It was a visit on the 19th of December that really confirmed Blank's illness for me, although it would be strange to call it an illness. An illness is something, though sad, that can be comprehended by the average human mind.
On that cold day in December, he told me of a strange palm figurine that he had found while walking on the road near New York. The figurine was very crudely carved, with facial features barely being recognizable. Yet, despite being an archeologist, one who had seen all kinds of different tribal art styles, I was not prepared for the atrocity that he held in his hand. The figurine had been covered in ash, that I could tell. However, the strange figurine harbored a look in its ill-carved eyes that filled me with a sensation of sickness. Apparently, Blank had indeed not acquired this monstrosity from any sort of curious shop or peddler or anything like that. As he said, it was simply found on a road that was downhill from the asylum fire that I mentioned earlier.
The worst part of the figurine which was only as large as my hand was not the look however. It was the smell. The smell, which seemed to originate from a discolored spot on the back of the head, reeked in a strange way. It was closer to the same sensation one may receive when eating a slice of Brie with the rind, but this felt absolutely intoxicating.
I went home and while walking through the snow, I though I saw prints in the ice that were much larger than mine. The sheer size of the prints and the gradual and shallow contour that they presented may have been mistaken for odd depressions in the snow that had nothing to do with a large animal, but I felt at the time that I could see them quite clearly.
It was later that my lifelong friend Blank disappeared. I had gone to visit his house one day, but found neither Blank nor anything in the vacant house. Absolutely nothing had been left behind. However, there was a strange purple syrup staining what remained of the floorboards, as well as an overwhelming stench much akin to the one I described earlier. I walked in through the broken door and before I knew it, the rotten floorboards creaked and give away. I feel around 8 feet and landed in the basement. In the basement, the stench was even stronger and the purple anomaly that I had noted earlier covered the concrete floor. I soon realized I was stuck.
As I desperately tried to move, strange roots began to manifest themselves on the walls. The light above me vanished, and soon, the basement grow cold. This is all I can say. Later, I found myself in a forest. No light came from the sky above. Instead, there was light generated from various fungi, enough to illuminate the way. Blank had told me stories of the parallel worlds that he sent letters to, but until that moment, I hadn't the slightest inkling that they were true. He told me of a great tree that grew in the gap between two islands, the tree being large enough to shroud the entire land it grew on. In this damp but comfortably cool atmosphere, I could feel the essence of nature returning, something being destroyed in the world I come from. This regeneration, combined with Blank's epic tales added to my fascination. Despite my amazement, there was a small part of me that felt unsettled, like something was amiss. For the sake of the world, I dare not say what.
It was the figurine, I later realized, that was one of many other figurines being carved in an unknown place in this forest world, and being transported to what we know as Earth. Although we humans think of time as a line that flows from one end to another, it's actually more complex than that. I realized this when I returned to Earth, except as a different man. I have been separated from everyone I once knew since. The power of the other worlds is a terrible thing. We will be powerless to stop any sort of dimensional or time-related atrocity that comes our way.
Since this discovery, I have become largely apathetic to any happenings, but I still wonder about Blank. Where did he go to? I heard from a friend of mine that he had turned up somewhere in China, so after receiving his address, I sent him a letter. He did not respond. After the asylum fire that took place in 1939, I stopped caring completely. I feel like one of a number, kind of like an empty shell...

Zeffon.title: The (nt) Fnl Bhg Stîcxk (No. 12 - ÛÛÛÛÛÛ baje-yield Eeze)
Zeffon.about:
Thinking silently to herself, Morgan began to consider two different anomalies that she had encountered in her otherwise quiet life, or rather, her life that had been very quiet up until that point. She had never known her mother, but she was affixed with a strange amount of fascination for this seemingly absent figure, as if she was on the cusp of remembering the kind words her mother spoke to her while she sat in the long grass, gazing through her peripheral vision at the reflection of the sun on pools of water that had been left behind by the recent rains.
As she progressed on her climb up a steeper part of the cliff face, she imagined herself in a woodland forest, with the mist rising from the dirt below tickling her bare feet. This imagery was mostly constructed to distract from the intense task at hand, and, after another hour or so, she had reached the top of the cliffside and was now present in what her ancestors had presumably called the Chaoslands. That said, a feeling of comfort and appreciation consumed Morgan as she walked into the dense forest that had overtaken the land not far from the cliffside, being isolated from mankind for ages. The sound of songbirds that she had never heard before and the view of the first true setting sun she had ever witnessed compounded the glory of such an experience. What a marvelous moment this was!
As she glanced at the setting sun in the west, she happened to avert her gaze slightly to the south, and there she very distantly another plateau that had once been an island, now a slab of rock protruding from the swirling mist of cloud patterns that obscured Kore-Ijra and its citizens far below. Squinting, she swore she could make out a figure with flowing red hair and brown eyes in very fine detail, one wearing leather armor and carrying a small pouch of saffron while planting corms. She turned towards Morgan, smiled, and waved. In disbelief that she could a figure in a field from this distance, Morgan rubbed her eyes and blinked twice, fearing there might've been some dust in them. When she tried a second time to see, Morgan only witnessed a sea of clouds.

Zeffon.title: The Sun Moves
Zeffon.about:
i. Corooe Mater
Ever since Unkardia sunk under the sea, most of civilization went with it. It was an odd time for humanity, as the Sharhodeon Forest migrated to the Seraph Territories and took root there. Soon, it expanded to cover the entire continent. Although it was interesting to see nature take its course and cover every single bit of the land, it became clear that this was permanent: there was no chance of civilization coming on the rise again.
ii. Primitive 2
I found my companion (a small robin whom I called Dawnish), after I saw Teran take the Forest Element from the Sharhodeon Forest. Robins supposedly hold the essence of Dränsilane, the strange man who lived 1000 years and shaped the very path of the universe. Despite what many believe, I think he was a good man, sacrificing his sanity for the sake of humanity, even if his lack of sanity did end up causing problems for everyone else.
iii. Sun, Part 1
My name is Ryan. I was in a deep sleep in a very dark place until I heard the sound of water. I suddenly leapt to my feet and ran out of the cave, a torrent of filthy water in my wake. However, by then it was too late. I was drowning in the Putrid Sea that was rushing into the space where Unkardia used to be. Then, something came from the depths of the water below me. I thought it was going to eat me, but it pushed me out of the waves with its nose, allowing me to reach the surface for air. I looked below me to see what it was, but it had already retreated. I tried to swim for a distance, but quickly grew tired and fainted.
iv. Bleed
When I awoke again, I was on a shore, which I only assumed could be the shoreline for the Chaoslands.
v. Red Sand
FREE ME FROM THESE BANDAGES.
vi. Shifting Wood
I’m not sure I quite understood, but I tried to the best of my ability.
The Isle of Origin became my new home when the world of Zeffon began to collapse. By collapse, I mean the ocean began to swallow all the land until there was nothing left.
vii. I Die
My name is Oscar. We live in a dimension that is called Revenence as far as I know – the name comes from an old text that was found when a portal to the new dimension was opened on Mount Jade. When the water from Zeffon began to creep through the portal, it was shut off. I left everything in Zeffon, including my companion, named Adelais Isga. I met Adelais when she rescued me from my low-lying village. We quickly became friends.
viii. Sun, Part 2
So far, there’s not much left of the old world, but supposedly, there is a place where people still live. There’s also an odd power emanating from the edges of the now-defunct portal, something that Adelais said that she feared. I have no idea why.
ix. Feeding the Birds out of a Bag
Somehow, my mother managed to make it into Revenence with me as well. Lately, she has fallen ill to something that none of the doctors here can diagnose. My sister Maya has had a difficult time with mother’s sickness, and has rarely left her side. I dearly hope that our mother will be able to pull through.
x. The Rotting Horned King, Part 1
Lydia, the only psychic mage to make it into Revenence, was nearly killed today. I didn’t see much, but a frail, fragile-looking man apparently entered her mind and caused her to cut off her hands. Despite supposedly being immortal, Lydia nearly died. The word is being spread that she passed on, but I know the truth.
xi. The Rotting Horned King, Part 2
As I sit here, I often think about the fate of the world, the fate of humanity... We are meant to survive forever, at least, until our promise to the lich is kept.
xii. Sun, Part 3
No one knows where the lich is now, but it is said that he made a pact with humanity to destroy the purple star in exchange for humanity's happiness. Though with a creature so uncommon as a lich, the promise of happiness seems increasingly unlikely.
Daylight crept in through the bandages, and I could see...
xiii. Tuhigpläfen
Something happened at Ter-El today. Ter-El is the town that was built when we passed into the dimension of Reverence. A tall man in a hood marched through town, asking passerby if they had seen someone named Lydia Isga. The townsfolk told him that Lydia Isga was dead. I think the person probably knew that Lydia was still alive – why would he have asked so many people the same question if he though Lydia was dead?
xiv. Zorer
A shrine was uncovered to the north of Ter-El today. It was covered in fallen trees and pine needles, as if the trees were deliberately placed there to hide the shrine. On a small pedestal, there was a book that described something that the elders of our town (and the elders of Zeffon) had always feared: The Curse of Ytrac was indeed real.
xv. Killing Field...! (Doom Tribute)
We are meant to live forever. Even if we die over and over in increasingly gruesome ways, humanity will always survive. Even if we commit ritual suicide as a species, humanity will always survive.
xvi. Dränsilane's Theme (Stone-Turning Words)
PROTECT US ALL.
xvii. The Great Flight, Part 2
It is too late.
xviii. The Sun Moves
We are already a part of the Earth...

trackinfo.title: Corooe Mater
trackinfo.lyrics: i. Corooe Mater Ever since Unkardia sunk under the sea, most of civilization went with it. It was an odd time for humanity, as the Sharhodeon Forest migrated to the Seraph Territories and took root there. Soon, it expanded to cover the entire continent. Although it was interesting to see nature take its course and cover every single bit of the land, it became clear that this was permanent: there was no chance of civilization coming on the rise again.
trackinfo.credits: from The Sun Moves, released April 11, 2017

trackinfo.title: Primitive 2
trackinfo.lyrics: ii. Primitive 2 I found my companion (a small robin whom I called Dawnish), after I saw Teran take the Forest Element from the Sharhodeon Forest. Robins supposedly hold the essence of Dränsilane, the strange man who lived 1000 years and shaped the very path of the universe. Despite what many believe, I think he was a good man, sacrificing his sanity for the sake of humanity, even if his lack of sanity did end up causing problems for everyone else.
trackinfo.credits: from The Sun Moves, released April 11, 2017

trackinfo.title: Sun, Part 1
trackinfo.lyrics: iii. Sun, Part 1 My name is Ryan. I was in a deep sleep in a very dark place until I heard the sound of water. I suddenly leapt to my feet and ran out of the cave, a torrent of filthy water in my wake. However, by then it was too late. I was drowning in the Putrid Sea that was rushing into the space where Unkardia used to be. Then, something came from the depths of the water below me. I thought it was going to eat me, but it pushed me out of the waves with its nose, allowing me to reach the surface for air. I looked below me to see what it was, but it had already retreated. I tried to swim for a distance, but quickly grew tired and fainted.
trackinfo.credits: from The Sun Moves, released April 11, 2017

trackinfo.title: Bleed
trackinfo.lyrics: iv. Bleed When I awoke again, I was on a shore, which I only assumed could be the shoreline for the Chaoslands.

trackinfo.title: Shifting Wood

trackinfo.credits: from The Sun Moves, released April 11, 2017

trackinfo.title: I Die
trackinfo.lyrics: vii. I Die My name is Oscar. We live in a dimension that is called Revenence as far as I know – the name comes from an old text that was found when a portal to the new dimension was opened on Mount Jade. When the water from Zeffon began to creep through the portal, it was shut off. I left everything in Zeffon, including my companion, named Adelais Isga. I met Adelais when she rescued me from my low-lying village. We quickly became friends.
trackinfo.credits: from The Sun Moves, released April 11, 2017

trackinfo.title: Sun, Part 2
trackinfo.lyrics: viii. Sun, Part 2 So far, there’s not much left of the old world, but supposedly, there is a place where people still live. There’s also an odd power emanating from the edges of the now-defunct portal, something that Adelais said that she feared. I have no idea why.
